label: SpecRequirement
text: All exercise and setup helpers are exported from testing.go in the kms external tests package, so other test files in the package reuse them instead of reimplementing the transit and PKI flows.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExercisePKIForKey drives the PKI certificate exercises for a single base name, delegating to the root, intermediate and CA exercise functions so a key backing PKI is validated for certificate issuance.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExercisePKIWithTransitKMS calls SetupPKI, then skips every key type from knownTransitKeyTypes whose SignVerify flag is false; for the remaining types it runs a parallel subtest named after the type that writes a backing key at keys/keys/pki-<type>, writes an external key config at sys/external-keys/configs/kms/keys/pki-<type> with name and version 1, and calls ExercisePKIForKey with the base name.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExercisePKICA exercises CA behaviour on the given PKI mount for the named issuer.

label: SpecInterface
name: ExerciseTransitSignVerify
signature: func ExerciseTransitSignVerify(t *testing.T, client *api.Client, mountName string, keyName string)

label: SpecInterface
name: ExercisePKIRootCA
signature: func ExercisePKIRootCA(t *testing.T, client *api.Client, mountName string, keyName string, extKeyRef string)

label: SpecInterface
name: ExerciseTransitForKey
signature: func ExerciseTransitForKey(t *testing.T, client *api.Client, baseName string, encryptDecrypt bool, signVerify bool)

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExerciseTransitForKey runs an "encrypt-decrypt" subtest only when the encryptDecrypt flag is set and a "sign-verify" subtest only when the signVerify flag is set; each subtest runs in parallel and invokes the corresponding exercise twice, once against the "keys" mount and once against the "transit" mount, with the base name as the key name.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SetupPKI prepares a PKI secrets engine on the client so the PKI exercise functions can issue certificates through it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SetupTransit mounts a secrets engine of type "transit" at the path "transit" through the client's Sys().Mount call and fails the test when the mount returns an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExercisePKIRootCA exercises root CA generation on the given PKI mount using the given key name and external key reference.

label: SpecInterface
name: ExercisePKICA
signature: func ExercisePKICA(t *testing.T, client *api.Client, mountName string, issuerName string)

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExerciseTransitWithTransitKMS first calls SetupTransit, then for every key type in knownTransitKeyTypes runs a subtest named after the type: it writes a backing key at keys/keys/transit-<type> with the type, writes an external key config at sys/external-keys/configs/kms/keys/transit-<type> with name and version 1, and then calls ExerciseTransitForKey with the base name and the type's EncryptDecrypt and SignVerify capabilities.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExerciseTransitForKey writes the transit key at transit/keys/<baseName> with type "external-key" and external_key_ref "kms:<baseName>" and requires that this write fails while no grant exists; it then creates the grant by writing sys/external-keys/configs/kms/keys/<baseName>/grants/transit, requires that write to succeed, and retries the same transit key write requiring success this time.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExerciseTransitSignVerify exercises sign and verify round trips against the given mount and key name, taking the client, mount name and key name as its inputs.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ExercisePKIIntermediateCA exercises intermediate CA generation and signing on the given PKI mount using the given key name and external key reference.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A read of kv/subkeys/foo for a path that was never written must fail with HTTP 404 Not Found.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After a secret is deleted, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must return HTTP 404 and a parsed body whose subkeys value is nil and whose metadata map carries a non-empty string deletion_time.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A JSONMergePatch issued with the cluster root token after writing {bar: baz, foo: qux} must set bar to "quux" and remove the foo key entirely, so a following read of kv/data/foo returns bar="quux" and a data map with no foo entry; a null value in the patch body deletes the key.

label: SpecRequirement
text: For the upgrade regression, the test must mount kv-v2, seal the cores with cluster.EnsureCoresSealed, delete the policy/ and archive/ subtrees beneath the KVv2 base path using logical.ClearView over physical.NewView on core.UnderlyingRawStorage, then unseal with testhelpers.EnsureCoresUnsealed, wait ten seconds, and fail if the captured hclog output contains "cannot write to storage during setup".

label: SpecRequirement
text: When the file audit backend records a write to kv/data/foo followed by a JSONMergePatch to the same path, decoding the audit log must yield exactly one record of type "request" and exactly one of type "response" whose request operation is "patch".

label: SpecRequirement
text: When multiple versions exist, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must succeed with HTTP 200 and the parsed subkeys value must deep-equal the nested key tree {foo: nil, bar: {a: {c: nil}, b: nil}, baz: nil}, so the endpoint returns only key structure of the current version and never the values.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After a secret version is destroyed, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must return HTTP 404 and a parsed body containing a subkeys key that is nil together with metadata whose destroyed flag is the boolean true.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test in the package must construct its backend through vault.NewTestCluster with a CoreConfig that registers the kv logical factory (logicalKv.VersionedKVFactory or logicalKv.Factory) and vaulthttp.Handler as the handler, start the cluster, wait for the core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive, and mount the versioned KV engine under the path "kv" with type "kv-v2" before exercising any endpoint.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A raw PATCH request to /v1/kv/data/foo sent with Content-Type "application/json" must be rejected with HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type, so that only a merge-patch media type is accepted by the KVv2 data endpoint.

label: SpecRequirement
text: kvRequestWithRetry must poll the supplied request closure once per second for at most twenty seconds and return as soon as the closure succeeds, tolerating repeated failures whose *api.ResponseError message contains "Upgrading from non-versioned to versioned data"; it must return the response and error unchanged for any other error, and must report "timeout expired waiting for upgrade" when the deadline is reached.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestLeaderReElectionMetrics requests GET /v1/sys/metrics with cluster.RootToken in the consts.AuthHeaderName header, reads and JSON-unmarshals the body into testhelpers.SysMetricsJSON, and errors when either the core.active or the core.unsealed gauge is absent or does not equal 1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After mounting a kv version 2 backend at path kv with version option 2, the same nonlocal logical core.mount_table.num_entries gauge equals 4 and core.mount_table.size stays non-zero; the test documents that on a transactional storage backend the size gauge reports only the new table entry, not a running total.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Before any user mount is added, the test asserts that the core.mount_table.num_entries gauge carrying labels local=false and type=logical equals 3, covering the cubbyhole, identity and kv mounts, and that the matching core.mount_table.size gauge is non-zero; a size of zero or less is a fatal failure.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After calling client.Sys().StepDown on the active core, the test waits for core 1 to report active and repeats the same GET /v1/sys/metrics assertions through the core 1 client, so the core.active and core.unsealed gauges must both be present and equal 1 on the new leader.

label: SpecRequirement
text: gaugeConditionCheck returns an error equality gauge check for comparison failed only when the comparator is the string eq and the two integers differ; any other comparator value passes without error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: gaugeSearchHelper returns the collected core.mount_table.size value on success; it selects only gauges whose local label is the string false and whose type label is the string logical, requires the core.mount_table.num_entries gauge to be seen and otherwise returns the sentinel max-int value together with the error No metrics reported for mount sizes, and returns the same sentinel together with an error when the entry gauge value fails the eq check against the expected value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestMountTableMetrics starts a two-core test cluster named mycluster with corehelpers.NewMockBuiltinRegistry as the builtin registry, vaulthttp.Handler as the handler, KeepStandbysSealed false, and a testhelpers.TestMetricSinkProvider sink on a one-minute interval, waits for core 0 to report active with vault.TestWaitActive before reading metrics, and defers cluster.Cleanup.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Listing identity/mfa/method globally must return a non-nil response whose keys entry and whose key_info map each contain exactly as many entries as the number of method configs created.

label: SpecRequirement
text: For each of the totp, duo, okta and pingid providers, writing a config to identity/mfa/method/<type> must return a non-empty method_id; reading identity/mfa/method/<type>/<method_id> must return the same id with namespace_id "root" and an empty namespace_path; listing identity/mfa/method/<type> must include that method id in keys; an update through the same id-bearing path must be visible on the next read; and reading the id through a different provider type path must fail.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing an empty login enforcement config must fail with an error whose text contains "missing method ids".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a login enforcement with mfa_method_ids but none of auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids or identity_entity_ids must fail with an error whose text contains "One of auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, identity_entity_ids must be specified".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a totp config to identity/mfa/method/totp/<id> for a method id that does not exist must fail with an error whose text contains "Code: 404".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a method config that carries method_name must return a method_id, and re-writing the same method_name must return the same method_id; writing a second config with a new name must succeed; updating an existing method to take another method's name must fail; and a method_name that contains a slash such as "ns1/<original>" must be accepted.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Reading identity/mfa/method/<method_id> without a provider type must return the method with its matching id, deleting an invalid path must fail, and after a successful delete on the id-bearing path a read must yield a nil response with a nil error (the 404 translation).

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a login enforcement to identity/mfa/login-enforcement/<name> must persist mfa_method_ids and auth_method_accessors such that a read returns equivalent slices, the name must appear in the list at identity/mfa/login-enforcement, a later write adding identity_group_ids and identity_entity_ids must be readable back as equivalent slices, and after delete the read must return nil response with nil error both immediately and after sealing and unsealing the cluster.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every test must build its cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler as the TestClusterOptions HandlerFunc, wait for the core to become active, clean the cluster on exit, and where a credential backend is needed register the userpass factory and enable auth at the userpass path before using its mount accessor.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The final phase of TestRecovery must restart the cluster against the same inmem HA backend with recovery mode off, SkipInit true and the previously captured barrier keys, unseal with testhelpers.EnsureCoresUnsealed, wait for active, list secret/ using the original root token, and fail if the listing returns any data other than nil, proving the raw delete performed in recovery mode persisted.

label: SpecRequirement
text: In recovery mode (CoreConfig.RecoveryMode true, TestClusterOptions.SkipInit true, handler properties RecoveryMode true and a RecoveryToken atomic.Value pointer), listing sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID> must fail with an error containing "403" both when the client token is "garbage" and when it is empty, and must still fail with "403" after a recovery operation token has been generated but before the client adopts it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each phase of TestRecovery should construct its own TestCluster with NumCores 1 and defer cluster.Cleanup, and should call cluster.EnsureCoresSealed before moving to the next phase, so the recovery and regular clusters never hold the storage backend open at the same time.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRecovery must generate a recovery operation token with testhelpers.GenerateRoot(t, cluster, testhelpers.GenerateRecovery) and must confirm that a second call through testhelpers.GenerateRootWithError with the same mode fails with the message "attempted to generate recovery operation token when already unsealed".

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRecovery must use a single inmem.NewInmemHA physical backend shared across all three phases, write map[string]any{"bar": 1.0} to secret/foo, assert that listing secret/ returns exactly the key "foo", capture the UUID of the secret/ mount and the UUID of a namespace created with Sys().CreateNamespace("ns1", nil), then seal the cores and save cluster.BarrierKeys for the later phases.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With the generated recovery token set on the client, TestRecovery must successfully list sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID> and see keys equal to []any{"foo"}, and must successfully delete sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID>/foo through client.Logical().Delete.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRecovery must list sys/raw/namespaces/<nsUUID> with the recovery token and require the returned data to contain a "keys" entry whose values include "core/".

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRecoverFromPanic must build a CoreConfig whose LogicalBackends map registers "noop" to backend.NoopBackendFactory and sets EnableRaw true, start a TestCluster with vaulthttp.Handler, mount a logical mount of type "noop" through core.Client.Sys().Mount, and then issue client.Logical().Read("noop/panic"), which must return a non-nil error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After the panicking read, TestRecoverFromPanic must wait for the core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive and then call cluster.EnsureCoresSealed(t), so a regression in panic recovery that prevents the core from sealing causes the test to deadlock rather than pass.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The listSecrets helper should return nil when the list response is nil, and otherwise decode the "keys" field with mapstructure into a []string so callers compare length only.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The restart helper must stop the first node, start it again with the original options, unseal all nodes, and wait for an active node; after the first restart the test must require that listing secret/ still returns at least one key.

label: SpecRequirement
text: In recovery mode the test must generate a recovery token with testcluster.GenerateRoot(cluster, testcluster.GenerateRecovery), must fail the test if a second GenerateRecovery call returns no error, and must then set the returned token on the client with SetToken.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test must start a Docker cluster with NumCores 1, image repo quay.io/openbao/openbao, tag latest, VaultBinary set to the BAO_BINARY value, node LogLevel TRACE, and must defer cluster cleanup.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With the recovery token set, the test must list sys/raw/logical/<secretMountUUID> and require its keys to equal [foo], then delete sys/raw/logical/<secretMountUUID>/foo through the raw storage endpoint.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Before any restart, the test must mount a kv-v1 engine at secret/, write secret/foo with value {"bar": 1.0}, list secret/ and require the keys to equal [foo], then read the mount list and record the UUID of the secret/ mount for later raw access.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After a final normal-mode restart, the test must require that listing secret/ returns zero keys, proving the raw deletion performed in recovery mode persisted across the restart.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The recovery-mode restart must stop the node, copy the original options, set Args to ["-recovery"], and start the node with a StartProbe that calls GenerateRecoveryOperationTokenStatusWithContext, because in recovery mode the only paths reachable without a recovery token are those used to generate one.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test may call t.Parallel() so it runs concurrently with other tests in the package.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRecovery_Docker must read the BAO_BINARY variable with api.ReadBaoVariable and skip the test with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when it is empty, so the Docker test never runs without an explicit binary.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestNamespaceClusterSealing runs a three-core test cluster in parallel and uses eventual assertions with 25 second timeouts and 100 millisecond polling for namespace creation, unsealing and resealing, because standby nodes can lag behind.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Unsealing a namespace from any core must unseal it immediately on the active core and eventually on all other nodes, and sealing a namespace must make it sealed again on all nodes.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestNamespaceRepeatedDeletion skips itself when the CI environment variable is non-empty, because creating 500 KV and userpass objects causes context cancellation timeouts, and otherwise runs in parallel.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Once the second delete is issued, sys/namespaces must become empty within the eventual timeout, and listing sys/raw/namespaces/<uuid> for the deleted namespace must return nil, showing namespace storage is gone.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Creating a namespace with a seal configuration must return a response carrying key_shares, and the Shamir configuration with shares 3 and threshold 2 must yield 3 share strings.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After the namespace is deleted and the active core is stepped down, the namespace must still appear under sys/namespaces, a read of sys/namespaces/ns1 must report tainted true, and a second delete must be accepted.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After cores are sealed, stepped down and unsealed, namespaces that were unsealed must become reachable again on all nodes, showing unsealed namespace state is synchronized when nodes rejoin.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A sealed namespace must reject mount listing with an error containing "is sealed" and a nil mount list on every core of the cluster, and an unsealed namespace must list non-empty mounts without error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Namespace population must enable KV-v2 mounts named kv-v2, kv-v1 and kv under the kv logical backend factory plus userpass credential backend, wait for the KV-v2 mount config to expose cas_required before writing entries, and write entries and users concurrently in the namespace of the admin policy.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both files declare package plugin_test so the tests exercise the internal vault, http and builtin plugin packages only through their exported API.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The auth-method and secrets-engine tests mount five instances of the same plugin in parallel subtests and complete a full lifecycle on each (configuration, credential or secret-id generation, login or read, renew and revoke or deregister), which requires the mounts to share a single multiplexed plugin process.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Tests for secret and auth plugins lazily load the mount, seal every core, unseal with all barrier keys, assert the core is not sealed, and wait for active so post-unseal plugin restoration is proven to complete.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When a file audit backend is enabled, audit records for requests and responses on an external auth or secret plugin mount must contain mount_class equal to the plugin type string, mount_is_external_plugin as boolean true, and mount_running_sha256 as a string.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The mock plugin entrypoints serve only when the SDK's plugin version environment variable is set, require the CA cert variable to be non-empty, parse the ca-cert flag, and dispatch to lplugin.Serve or lplugin.ServeMultiplex with a mock factory for the logical or credential backend type; the V4 variants additionally return early when AutoMTLS is enabled and install a TLSProviderFunc.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The shared helpers register a compiled plugin in the catalog with its name, type, command, sha256 and version, then enable it either as a secrets mount (Sys().Mount) for consts.PluginTypeSecrets or as an auth method (Sys().EnableAuthWithOptions) for consts.PluginTypeCredential, and fail the test on any error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Reload is asserted both on the per-plugin endpoint and on the sys/plugins/reload/backend endpoint: after writing an internal value of baz and issuing the reload (by plugin name or by mounts list), a subsequent read must return a value other than baz and the backend endpoint response must carry a non-nil reload_id.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After a credential or secret plugin is registered, configured and used, calling ReloadPlugin on it must succeed and the same auth method or secret read must still work, after which the plugin is deregistered.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The database plugin test mounts an external database secrets engine, prepares a PostgreSQL 13.4-buster test container with a vault user, writes a connection config bound to the plugin name, rotates the root credential, creates a role from the templated creation statements, generates credentials, and requires that a lease lookup succeeds before revocation and fails after it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The external plugin continue-on-error test runs all four combinations of failure kind (sha256 mismatch via catalog update, missing binary via file removal) and plugin type (secret, auth), then seals and unseals, recompiles and re-registers the plugin, and requires that the previously failed unmount or auth disable now succeeds.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Removing the plugin binary from the cluster temp directory and unsealing must make a later read of sys/mounts/mock-0/tune fail, and deleting the plugin from the catalog, sealing and unsealing must leave the cluster active; when the test re-adds the plugin and mounts it on the still-existing path, that mount must fail.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A read of the mock plugin's errors/rpc path must return an error and must reset the backend's in-memory internal value, proving automatic reload after an RPC failure.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestExternalPlugin_DatabaseReload skips with the message that reloading database plugins is not yet supported, so database reload remains explicitly unsupported until that skip is removed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Plugin behaviour is asserted for each protocol generation by the logicalVersionMap and credentialVersionMap tables, whose keys v4, v5 and v5_multiplexed select the mock plugin entrypoint (V4, plain Serve, or ServeMultiplex) that the test registers for that generation.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The env test mounts a plugin registered with FOO=BAR in its environment and the mock plugin entrypoint fails unless os.Getenv("FOO") equals BAR, confirming the plugin process receives the configured environment alongside the CA certificate variable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Adding the entity to the previously empty foobar group MUST make the path templated on that group name resolve: a write to secret/foobar/foo that was denied before the membership change MUST succeed afterwards.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPolicyTemplating MUST accept identity-templated paths over entity name, entity metadata keys, group names, group ids, and alias names. Given an entity named entity_name with metadata key=metadata, a group named group_name containing that entity, a group named foobar, and a userpass alias named testuser, writes to secret/entity_name/foo, secret/group_name/foo, secret/<groupID>/foo, secret/testuser/foo and secret/metadata/test/foo MUST succeed, while a write to secret/entityname/foo MUST be denied.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Entity metadata whose value contains template-breaking characters, a wildcard, MUST make every templated path in the policy fail. Rewriting the same policy with allow_wildcards_in_identity_templates and allow_slashes_in_identity_templates both true MUST restore access without changing the metadata.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPolicy_TokenRenewal MUST run four table cases (no policies, token policies only, identity policies only, both) by enabling the userpass auth backend, optionally setting token_policies on the user, optionally creating an identity entity with policies plus an entity-alias bound through the userpass mount accessor, and logging in. The login response MUST report Auth.TokenPolicies equal to the token policies with "default" prepended, Auth.IdentityPolicies equal to the configured identity policies, and Auth.Policies equal to the concatenation of both. After a renew through auth/token/renew the same three sets MUST be reported unchanged.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A policy that references a non-existent group through a name template MUST NOT prevent the other paths in the token's policy set from working. Installing badPolicy1, which templates identity.groups.names.foobar.name, MUST leave every other templated path behaving exactly as it did before, so only the unresolvable-template path is affected.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The LDAP-backed no-default-policy and no-configured-policy tests SHOULD remain commented out with their rationale recorded, so the package compiles and runs without an LDAP plugin or container while the intended coverage stays visible.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPolicyStore_DisabledCacheInvalidation MUST start a two-core cluster with DisableCache true, create a namespace, and write a read-only policy through the active core. It MUST then retry for up to 10 seconds against the standby core's GetPolicy until the returned policy text is byte-identical to the text that was written, so that policy writes invalidate on a standby when no cache is present.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The testPagination helper MUST assert, for a given metadata sub-path, that a raw list returns 100 keys when the path is unpaginated or at most 10 when paginated and errors when the path is not raw-listable, that a list page of 75 errors when the path is paginated and otherwise returns exactly 75 keys, and that a list page of 10 always succeeds with at most 10 keys. The limited and raw arguments decide which of these assertions apply.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPolicy_PaginationLimit MUST mount a versioned KV backend and write 100 keys under each of the a, b, c and d prefixes, then write a policy where kv/metadata/a allows list with no pagination limit, kv/metadata/b allows list with pagination_limit 10, kv/metadata/c allows list with required_parameters ["limit"] but no pagination limit, kv/metadata/d allows list with both pagination_limit 10 and required_parameters ["limit"], and kv/metadata/ allows scan and list with both settings. A raw list MUST return all 100 keys on a, c and the no-suffix path, and at most 10 keys on b; raw list on d MUST fail. A list with limit=max or limit=0 MUST return 10 keys where a pagination limit applies and 100 keys where none applies, and limit=-1 MUST fail with "permission denied". Scan without limits MUST error, scan with a page size of 10 MUST succeed and return 400 keys because KV metadata scanning does not paginate.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPostgreSQL_Scalability must build a PostgreSQL cluster storage with a node mapper that places the first two nodes on the primary, adds a replica for the third index and points later indices at the first replica, then start a three core OpenBao cluster with audit logging to stdout and trace level; it must verify a kv version 2 value is read identically from every node with client redirects disabled, and then in order require that sealing the primary lets a secondary accept writes, that the value propagates to the third node, that sealing the secondary makes the read-only third node fail with 'local node not active but active cluster node not found', that UnsealAllNodes restores identical reads everywhere, that removing the PostgreSQL primary makes writes and reads on the first node fail within thirty seconds, that the third node eventually reads the last written value, and that PromoteNode on the replica lets the remaining nodes write and read post-failover-known-value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPostgreSQL_Upgrade must first start a three node cluster on the published latest image with no binary override, mount a version 2 kv secrets engine, write the value known-value at a/key and wait for the write to succeed, then set VaultBinary on the options and call node.Upgrade on every node under a sixty second timeout; afterwards it must wait for an active node and require that reading a/key returns known-value again.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPostgreSQL_ParallelInit must copy the self-init.hcl and static-seal.hcl fixtures into the cluster config path, start with SkipInit set, require that the first node reports Initialized true and Sealed false, log in as admin through auth/userpass to adopt the returned auth token as the cluster root token, and then require that every node answers ListPoliciesWithContext within ten seconds so the count of active nodes equals the node count.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPostgreSQL_FatalInit must build the cluster directly through docker.NewDockerCluster with a single core, SkipInit true, an explicit cluster name derived from the test name and SkipStorageCleanup true, supply the failing self-init-failure.hcl fixture alongside the good ones, and require an error from the call; it must then swap the fixture set back to the working self-init.hcl and static-seal.hcl and require that startup is still refused with an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The file must declare package raft_binary, and every test must read the BAO_BINARY environment variable via api.ReadBaoVariable and call t.Skip when the value is empty, so no test reaches Docker unless a server binary path is supplied.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestPostgreSQL_FencedWrites must start a PostgreSQL-backed Docker cluster from the supplied binary, spam ten goroutines that each write sys/policies/acl/custom up to five hundred times with a 5ms pause, then delete every row from the openbao_ha_locks table through the storage client and require that at least one goroutine observed an error containing physical.ErrFencedWriteFailed; after a six second pause it must require testcluster.WaitForActiveNode to find a new active node and require that a repeat write on that node succeeds with a nil response.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each pprof response body must be read in full; an unmarshal error is ignored because some endpoints return binary blobs, but a response whose decoded JSON contains an errors key must fail the test with that error value, and an empty body must fail the test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SysPprof_Standby_Test must read sys/pprof/cmdline as a raw logical response from node 0 and then node 1 of the cluster, requiring no error and a non-empty command line from each and logging both values.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SysPprof_Test must exercise the sys/pprof endpoints index, cmdline, goroutine, heap, profile, symbol and trace, issuing one GET request per case against the first node of the cluster and running each as its own subtest named after the case.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The requests must go through an HTTP client built on cleanhttp's default pooled transport carrying the first node's TLS config, configured for HTTP/2, and any transport configuration error must fail the test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Go tests in pprof_test.go should call the exported helpers with a freshly created test cluster, so TestSysPprof drives SysPprof_Test and TestSysPprof_Standby drives SysPprof_Standby_Test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The profile and trace cases must send a seconds parameter of 1, and cases whose seconds value is empty must send no seconds parameter at all.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestSysPprof_Exec runs in parallel and, when the BAO_BINARY variable is non-empty, builds a dev cluster through testcluster.NewTestExecDevCluster with ClusterOptions.NumCores set to 1, BinaryPath taken from BAO_BINARY, and BaseListenAddress 127.0.0.1:8208, then calls pprof.SysPprof_Test with that cluster.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both tests read BAO_BINARY through api.ReadBaoVariable and call t.Skip with "only running exec test when $BAO_BINARY present" when the value is empty, so no cluster is started and no pprof assertion runs without a server binary; there are no command-line flags in this package.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestSysPprof_Standby_Exec runs in parallel and, when BAO_BINARY is non-empty, builds an exec dev cluster with VaultNodeConfig.DisablePerformanceStandby set to true, BinaryPath from BAO_BINARY, and BaseListenAddress 127.0.0.1:8210, then calls pprof.SysPprof_Standby_Test with that cluster.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package holds no pprof assertions of its own; the pprof response checks stay in the imported pprof package and are reached only through pprof.SysPprof_Test and pprof.SysPprof_Standby_Test, so the exec wrapper stays a thin transport-swap layer over the in-process tests.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test defers cluster.Cleanup() immediately after the cluster is created, so the spawned server process tree is torn down on pass, fail, or skip of the delegated pprof test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A global inheritable quota of 7.7 RPS must bound requests issued from the root and from namespace ns1, while a quota declared at path ns1/ns1.1 with 9.9 RPS must allow more requests, bounded by ceil(10 + 9.9*elapsedSeconds) + 1, when listing sys/namespaces inside ns1/ns1.1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test must build its own in-memory Vault cluster from teststorage.ClusterSetup with coreConfig, start it, wait for active with vault.TestWaitActive, and defer cluster.Cleanup; coreConfig must register the pki logical backend, the userpass credential backend and the file audit backend.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Creating a second rate-limit quota whose path collides with an existing quota's path (for example a global quota with empty path, then another empty-path quota) must be rejected with an error, and reading a quota by name must return non-empty data.

label: SpecRequirement
text: testRPS and testRPSWithNS must call the supplied request function in a tight loop until the given duration elapses, counting successes and failures in atomic counters, optionally setting and clearing a namespace per call, and must return the success count, the failure count and the elapsed wall-clock duration.

label: SpecRequirement
text: setupMounts must enable a userpass auth mount with user foo password bar, mount pki, generate an internal root certificate with common_name testvault.com, ttl 200h and ip_sans 127.0.0.1, and create role test with require_cn false, allowed_domains testvault.com, allow_subdomains true, max_ttl 2h and generate_lease true; teardownMounts must unmount pki and disable the userpass and approle auth mounts, failing the test on any error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A global rate-limit quota of 7.7 RPS must cause some requests to fail with successes bounded by ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after one second of refill and an update to 10000 RPS, no further request may fail.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A rate-limit quota with path pki/ at 7.7 RPS must reject some requests while keeping successes at or below ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after updating the same quota to 10000 RPS no request may fail; teardownMounts must then remove the mounts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With a rate-limit quota of 1 RPS in force, two consecutive reads of sys/health must both succeed and return non-nil responses with non-nil data, because sys/health belongs to the default exempt paths.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With enable_rate_limit_audit_logging true in sys/quotas/config and the file audit backend enabled, a first request must pass and a second request under a 1 RPS quota must fail with an error containing 429, and the audit log must contain exactly one request-type record whose error field ends with quotas.ErrRateLimitQuotaExceeded.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Default configuration read from sys/quotas/config must report a non-empty rate_limit_exempt_paths list; with a 7.7 RPS quota some requests must fail and successes must not exceed ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after writing rate_limit_exempt_paths containing sys/quotas/rate-limit and allowing one second for refill, every request must succeed and none must fail.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A quota on path ns1 with inheritable true at 7.7 RPS must apply to the child namespace ns1/ns1.1 so some requests there fail; after the same quota is rewritten with inheritable false, requests inside ns1/ns1.1 must all succeed while requests in ns1 must again fail under the same success bound.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Tests that opt in by setting RequestResponseCallback to schema.ResponseValidatingCallback must have every API response validated against the registered response schema; tests that disable default quotas set NoDefaultQuotas to keep the fixture free of built-in quota rules.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When a root rate-limit quota of 14.7 RPS and a pki/-scoped quota of 7.7 RPS both exist, the pki/-scoped quota must take precedence: some pki requests must fail and successes must stay at or below the bound computed from 7.7 RPS, not from 14.7.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a rate-limit quota at sys/quotas/rate-limit/secret-rlq twice under the same name with different paths must succeed and leave exactly one entry returned by listing sys/quotas/rate-limit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The helper builds the set of observed node_id values and an expected set of names core-0 through core-(N-1), where N is len(cluster.Nodes()), and fails the test when deep.Equal between the two sets returns a non-empty diff, reporting the diff with t.Fatalf.

label: SpecRequirement
text: For every server entry in secret.Data["config"]["servers"], the helper reads node_id and leader; the entry whose node_id is core-0 must have leader true, and every other entry must have leader false. A violation fails the test with t.Fatalf carrying the offending server value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Raft_Configuration_Test takes a *testing.T and a testcluster.VaultCluster, takes the API client of the cluster's first node via cluster.Nodes()[0].APIClient(), and reads the path sys/storage/raft/configuration with Logical().Read; a read error is reported with t.Fatal and stops the test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The assertion lives in raft.go and is driven from the package's test files: raft_test.go calls Raft_Configuration_Test from TestRaft_Configuration, so the helper stays free of test-registration side effects and remains callable by other tests in third_party/openbao/internal/vault/external_tests/raft/raft_autopilot_test.go and raft_test.go.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The cluster is built from a docker.DockerClusterOptions value with ImageRepo "quay.io/openbao/openbao", ImageTag "latest", VaultBinary set to the BAO_BINARY value, and ClusterOptions.VaultNodeConfig.LogLevel "TRACE", then that options value is passed to docker.NewTestDockerCluster along with the testing.T.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test calls t.Parallel() before any other setup, and defers cluster.Cleanup() immediately after docker.NewTestDockerCluster returns, so docker clusters do not leak when the test fails or is skipped over later.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRaft_Configuration_Docker reads api.ReadBaoVariable("BAO_BINARY") into a binary variable and calls t.Skip with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when that variable is empty, so the docker test runs only where a binary path is provided.

label: SpecRequirement
text: rafttest.Raft_Configuration_Test runs against the cluster once before cluster.AddNode, and again after AddNode succeeds; AddNode is called with the context from t.Context() and the same options value, and a non-nil error return fails the test with t.Fatal and prevents the second run.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After joining, testhelpers.VerifyRaftPeers on the leader client must confirm core-0, core-1 and core-2 are all present as peers.

label: SpecRequirement
text: testRaftHANewCluster must configure a vault.CoreConfig and vault.TestClusterOptions through teststorage.RaftHASetup with vaulthttp.Handler, start a three-core vault test cluster, and clean it up on exit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing sys/storage/raft/remove-peer with server_id core-1 and then core-2 against the leader client must succeed, and a following testhelpers.VerifyRaftPeers must confirm core-0 is the only remaining peer.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRaft_HA_NewCluster must run four parallel subtests: the file backend and the in-memory backend, each with and without client certificates, and each must delegate to testRaftHANewCluster with the matching teststorage bundler and addClientCerts flag.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The existing-cluster test should run with performance standby disabled, standbys kept sealed, and standby reads disabled, and should name its logger after the test for readable output.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Cores 1 and 2 must join through api.RaftJoinRequest carrying the cluster CA certificate as LeaderCACert, and when addClientCerts is true also carrying LeaderClientCert and LeaderClientKey from the cluster CA material; a join error or a response with Joined false must fail the test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: In the upgraded cluster the leader client must set the saved root token, seal the leader to install the address provider and unseal it again, write sys/storage/raft/bootstrap to make the leader active, install the address provider on the other two cores' raft backends, join cores 1 and 2 with the cluster CA certificate, and verify all three cores are peers.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestRaft_HA_ExistingCluster must create a cluster with raft absent as HA backend (physBundle.HABackend set to nil) over reusable in-memory storage, capture the cluster barrier keys and root token, then build a second cluster over reusable raft HA storage with SkipInit true and restore those captured barrier keys and root token onto it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The leader core must be sealed before a testhelpers.TestRaftServerAddressProvider is installed on its raft.RaftBackend, then unsealed, and the test must wait for the core to become active; this ordering exists because the address provider can only be swapped while the core is sealed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Header assertions must inspect the raw HTTP response through client.Logical().ReadRaw, which returns the status code and the header collection directly rather than the decoded logical response.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After client.Sys().TuneMount("auth/headtest", api.MountConfigInput{AllowedResponseHeaders: []string{"WwW-AuthenTicate"}}), the www-authenticate header value Negotiate must appear on both the 200 response from auth/headtest/loginnoerror and the 401 response from auth/headtest/login, so the allowed-list comparison must ignore letter case.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When the mount has not been tuned, reading auth/headtest/loginnoerror must return HTTP status 200 with an empty www-authenticate header, and reading auth/headtest/login must return an error with HTTP status 401 and an empty www-authenticate header; the test fails if any of these headers is present.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test registers a credential backend named headtest whose login and loginnoerror read callbacks each return a logical.Response carrying Headers map[string][]string with key www-authenticate and value Negotiate; login additionally returns logical.CodedError(401, "authentication required") and loginnoerror returns an empty logical.Auth with a nil error. The backend is mounted through the API as auth type headtest on a test cluster built from vault.CoreConfig with that factory.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test must run against a vault.NewTestCluster configured with HandlerFunc vaulthttp.Handler and DisableStandbyReads true, start it with cluster.Start(), wait for the active core with vault.TestWaitActive, and defer cluster.Cleanup() so the cluster is always torn down.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Mounting an auth backend and a secrets backend at nested subpath mount points must succeed whether the longer mounted path is created before or after the shorter one; the test runs the pair {"a/abcd/123", "abcd/123"} in both orders against a fresh cluster.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The failing-rollback test must mount the noop backend built from backend.NoopBackendRollbackErrFactory so the periodic rollback error is produced by the mounted backend itself.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Remounting a backend whose periodic rollback function returns an error must succeed: a write to sys/remount moving that mount to a new path must not return an error, and the cores must then seal and unseal.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After the auth and secrets backends are mounted at their subpaths, all cores in the cluster must seal and then unseal successfully, with a failure reported through the test rather than ignored.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Reloading a mounted backend whose periodic rollback function returns an error must succeed: a write to sys/plugins/reload/backend for that mount must not return an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both tests must build the cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler as the handler func, wait for the first core to become active, drive it through cluster.Cores[0].Client, and clean the cluster up on exit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: InitializeTransit must build a test cluster whose seal is a transit seal backed by the given TransitSealServer and seal key name, and must return both the started cluster and the TestClusterOptions used to create it so callers can reach the seal and unwrap seal functions.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14 must initialize a transit-sealed cluster, move the existing SealFunc into UnwrapSealFunc and set SealFunc to return nil, run the post-1.4 migration with the recovery keys, validate that the resulting seal configuration is shamir, then stop the transit server and run the cluster with shamir.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every ParamTest* scenario must accept the same parameter set — *testing.T, hclog.Logger, teststorage.ReusableStorage and an int base port — so a caller can run each scenario against any reusable storage backend with its own logger and port.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14 must initialize a cluster with shamir, capture root token and barrier keys, start a transit seal server holding key transit-seal-key-1, run the pre-1.4 shamir-to-transit migration where the barrier keys become recovery keys, then run the cluster in autoseal mode with the returned seal function.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package's test files should invoke the shared parameterized scenarios rather than reimplementing migration steps, with seal_migration_pre14_test.go covering the pre-1.4 path and seal_migration_test.go covering the post-1.4 and transit-to-transit paths.

label: SpecInterface
name: ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14
signature: func ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14(t *testing.T, logger hclog.Logger, storage teststorage.ReusableStorage, basePort int)

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Pre14 must start a transit seal server, create the key named transit-seal-key, initialize a cluster sealed with transit, ensure its cores are sealed, run the pre-1.4 transit-to-shamir migration, then stop the transit server and run the cluster with shamir using the former recovery keys as barrier keys.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParamTestSealMigration_TransitToTransit must exercise a seal migration from one transit seal to another, taking the logger, reusable storage and base port a caller supplies.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Post14 must initialize a shamir cluster, start a transit server with key transit-seal-key-1, replace opts.SealFunc with one that builds a seal from that transit server, run the post-1.4 migration with the barrier keys as recovery keys, validate that the seal configuration is transit, then run the cluster in autoseal mode.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test must build its logger with logging.NewVaultLogger at hclog.Debug level and rename it with t.Name(), so log records carry the test name.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestSealMigration_TransitToShamir_Post14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14 with BasePort_TransitToShamir_Post14 plus 300, mirroring the pre-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test at a different port base.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package must expose exactly five top-level tests, one for each seal-migration scenario: Shamir-to-Transit before 1.4, Transit-to-Shamir before 1.4, Shamir-to-Transit after 1.4, Transit-to-Shamir after 1.4 and Transit-to-Transit after 1.4.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test must obtain storage by calling teststorage.MakeReusableStorage with a backend produced by teststorage.MakeInmemBackend, and must defer the cleanup function that MakeReusableStorage returns so the storage is torn down when the test ends.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every test must pass a port derived from a sealmigration base-port constant plus 300: BasePort_ShamirToTransit_Pre14 for the pre-1.4 Shamir-to-Transit test, BasePort_TransitToShamir_Pre14 for the pre-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test, BasePort_TransitToShamir_Post14 for the post-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test and BasePort_TransitToTransit for the Transit-to-Transit test, so parallel runs on shared storage do not collide on listening ports.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test must delegate the scenario body to the matching parameterized helper in the sealmigration package, passing the logger, the storage handle and a base port, rather than implementing migration steps itself.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestSealMigration_ShamirToTransit_Pre14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14, while TestSealMigration_ShamirToTransit_Post14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14, which is the helper the file actually wires to that test name.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Transit-to-Transit scenario must run only in its post-1.4 form, through sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigration_TransitToTransit, with no pre-1.4 counterpart in this package.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every test in the package must call t.Parallel() before doing any other work, so the scenarios run concurrently.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The test cluster must reach a state with an active node and standbys before assertions run: after cluster.Start() and testhelpers.WaitForActiveNodeAndStandbys, cluster.Cores[0].Standby() must be false, and cleanup must be registered via t.Cleanup(cluster.Cleanup).

label: SpecRequirement
text: A value written through any core's KVv2 client into the kv mount must become readable through both the primary client and the standby client, polled with require.EventuallyWithT at a 10 second timeout and 100 millisecond tick, with the exact per-core expected value compared against data.Data["bar"].

label: SpecRequirement
text: For a ReadOperation carrying logical.RequestWrapInfo with a 15 second TTL, a core whose HAState() is consts.Active must return no error and a non-nil response whose WrapInfo.TTL equals 15 seconds, while every other core must return an error for which logical.ShouldForward(err) is true.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Standby nodes should handle requests that they cannot serve themselves by returning a forwardable error rather than executing the request locally, so callers can detect the condition with logical.ShouldForward.

label: SpecRequirement
text: After the primary revokes the token tree, the standby client must eventually fail its KVv2 read with an error containing "permission denied", showing that secondary nodes honor revocation performed on the primary.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The exercised storage contract must hold: the empty prefix is the root; Delete of a missing key succeeds; Get of a missing key returns a nil entry and no error; Put then Get returns the stored value; List of a key with children returns both the key and its trailing-slash subtree entry; Delete of a parent removes only the base entry and leaves children; repeated writes to one key return the last value even when shorter; and deleting all entries leaves no list artifacts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every backend in the map passed to exerciseBackends must return identical values for the same Get, Put, Delete, List and ListPage call, and deep.Equal differences must fail the test with a message naming the two backends and the differing items.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A transaction begun by BeginTx or BeginReadOnlyTx that is committed or rolled back with no intervening operations must succeed once, and the same terminal operation repeated on the finished transaction must fail regardless of whether the second operation is Commit or Rollback or swaps between them.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ListPage must return at most limit entries sorted lexicographically past after, with limit of zero or a negative integer meaning unlimited; after need not exist; an after value beyond all keys returns nothing; and pagination must be tested exhaustively for ten sequentially created key-N entries.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When shouldError is false each backend must return no error and when true each must return an error; the allDoSame* wrappers assert this per backend name before comparing results.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Two concurrent transactions that write the same key must conflict so the second terminal commit fails and the first committed value stands, including when both wrote byte-identical contents or one read then deleted the other's key; transactions writing disjoint keys must both commit and both values must be readable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: allLogical must supply map entries named pure-raft, raft, raft-in-tx, file, inmem, inmem-via-wrapper, txinmem-via-wrapper and psql, each begun via logical.NewLogicalStorage over the corresponding physical backend, and allTransactionalLogical must supply raft, txinmem, inmem+sv, inmem+aes+sv, inmem+aes+bv, inmem+cache+encoding+aes+bv and raft+cache+encoding+aes+bv.

label: SpecRequirement
text: getRandomOps must generate the configured operation counts (1000 for the non-transactional run, 1000 with a transaction limit of 10 for the transactional run) over the fixed file, folder, after and content operand sets, and the executors must serialize the ops to a JSON file under the system temporary directory, delete that file when the run finishes, and fail if any backend disagrees on error presence, list result or entry result.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Put and Delete on a read-only transaction must fail while Commit of that same transaction must succeed, and listing the underlying storage afterwards must show no change.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A nil list result and an empty list result must be treated as equal; the list and list-page comparisons skip the deep.Equal check when both expected and actual have length zero, because the file backend returns an empty slice where other backends return nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each top-level test must call t.Parallel, must defer the cleanup returned with the backend set, and must roll back every transaction-backed entry after exercising it so the shared raft and postgres resources are left usable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The ALPN scenario installs a DNS resolver on the cluster network for dadgarcorp.com, adds A records for openbao.dadgarcorp.com and invalid.dadgarcorp.com pointing at the container IP, pushes the config, writes pki/config/acme with enabled true and the resolver's remote address, expects certificate acquisition to succeed for openbao.dadgarcorp.com:443 and to fail for invalid.dadgarcorp.com:443.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test builds DockerClusterOptions against image quay.io/openbao/openbao with tag latest, sets VaultBinary to the value of BAO_BINARY, sets Entrypoint to the result of entrypointPath, uses one core, and passes TRACE log level plus the scenario's AdditionalListeners into VaultNodeConfig, then starts the cluster with docker.NewTestDockerCluster and defers cluster.Cleanup.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each scenario declares an additional plain TCP listener with tls_disable true to serve as the ACME directory server and an additional TCP listener with tls_acme_cache_path /tmp and tls_acme_ca_directory pointing at that directory server; the ALPN and non-privileged scenarios additionally set tls_acme_disable_http_challenge true with tls_acme_domains []string{"openbao.dadgarcorp.com"}, and the non-privileged scenario sets tls_acme_alpn_challenge_port 8222 and tls_acme_challenge_host 127.0.0.1 to avoid root.

label: SpecRequirement
text: setupPki mounts a pki secrets engine with 16h default and 32h max lease TTL and allowed response headers Last-Modified, Replay-Nonce, Link and Location, writes pki/config/cluster with both path and aia_path set to http://127.0.0.1 followed by the scenario's ACME port plus /v1/pki, enables pki/config/acme, generates an internal EC root named root with common name "Root R1", and returns the generated certificate string.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The privileged and ALPN scenarios set Root true so the container can bind ports 80 and 443, while the non-privileged scenario sets Root false and instead publishes container port 8443 as host port 443 through PublishPorts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: entrypointPath derives the Docker entrypoint from the calling source file using runtime.Caller(0) and joins the file's directory with ../../../../.release/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh; when runtime.Caller reports not ok it logs that it is assuming a path and returns the same relative path unresolved.

label: SpecRequirement
text: validateTLS builds and runs an Alpine image containing curl with the expected root certificate written to /root.pem, joins it to the cluster's container network, optionally rewrites /etc/resolv.conf with a search domain of dadgarcorp.com and the supplied nameserver, then runs curl --verbose --cacert /root.pem against https://<address>/v1/sys/health and fails the test when the command's non-zero return code disagrees with the expectFail argument.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each test waits for an active node with testcluster.WaitForActiveNode under a context bounded by a 60 second timeout, requires no error and a non-nil node, and obtains the API client from cluster.ClusterNodes[node].APIClient().

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every test function other than the helpers reads the BAO_BINARY variable through api.ReadBaoVariable and calls t.Skip with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when that variable is empty, so the suite is a no-op unless a built binary path is supplied.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The non-privileged scenario points the openbao.dadgarcorp.com A record at the container gateway IP so the ACME server reaches the listener through Docker's host 443 to container 8443 mapping.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_Roles_Batch covers token roles whose tokens are issued as batch tokens and asserts the resulting token type and role-derived policies.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_CreateOrphanResponse creates an orphan token with the default policy and fails unless the returned secret's Auth.Orphan field is true.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_RevocationOnStartup creates tokens and leases, restarts the core, unseals it, and fails unless the remaining lease count and token count match the expected leftovers after startup revocation.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestBatchToken_ParentLeaseRevoke creates a batch token from a leased parent credential and fails unless revoking the parent lease makes the batch token unusable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_CIDRBlocks exercises token creation with bound CIDR blocks and asserts the request from inside and outside the bound ranges succeeds or is denied accordingly.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestBatchTokens configures the cluster with the kv leased passthrough logical backend and the approle credential backend, mounts kv, writes a leased secret and a read-only policy, then creates, looks up and renews tokens and asserts the batch token type behavior exposed by consts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every test builds its own in-memory cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler and vault.TestClusterOptions, calls cluster.Start(), defers cluster.Cleanup(), and waits for the first core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive before issuing API calls.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_StandbyInvalidation creates a token, requires a non-empty client token, then uses require.EventuallyWithT to poll lookup-self and fails unless the reported ttl crosses the cutoff in the expected direction, and likewise for the renewable flag on the other token class.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_IdentityPolicies asserts that a token created against an identity receives exactly the expected identity policies, and fails when identity_policies is set on a token that should not carry any.

label: SpecRequirement
text: TestTokenStore_TokenInvalidEntityID mounts the userpass credential backend and fails when a token whose backing entity is invalid is accepted instead of rejected with an error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both test files declare package token and live in the directory third_party/openbao/internal/vault/external_tests/token, forming one compiled Go test package of external tests.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The context must expose no exported interface: the observed facts list the file alone and no function, type, method, constant or variable, so other packages may depend on this path only as a test target and never import a symbol from it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The repository must carry third_party/openbao/internal/vault/external_tests/userpass_binary/ip_token_binding_test.go as part of the userpass_binary external test set, so that the IP-token-binding behavior of the userpass auth method has a dedicated test file inside the vendored tree.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The acceptance test creates a separate child namespace for each subtest (acceptance, recursion, mfa, unauthenticated, alias-lookahead) and runs that subtest against a client scoped with WithNamespace, so the subtests do not share workflow or auth state.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Executing the create-namespace workflow with namespace, username and password inputs creates the namespace, mounts userpass auth, writes an ns-admin ACL policy, creates the named user, mounts kv-v2 at secret, and returns output containing the input namespace and an auth client_token.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Workflow definitions must support template-evaluated request paths built from input fields and response field selectors, eval of data values from inputs, and output data drawn from a named flow's named response field selector, including sourcing the authentication flow's auth.client_token.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The token returned by the create-namespace workflow must be usable in the newly created child namespace to write and read a kv-v2 secret at secret/data/test.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With AllowUnauthenticatedWorkflows false, a tokenless client must receive a "permission denied" error from sys/workflows/unauthed-execute even for a workflow stored with allow_unauthenticated true.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A workflow whose authentication flow uses the alias-lookahead operation must exist and be listable, but executing it through sys/workflows/execute must fail with an error containing "cannot handle internal-only request operation" and return no response.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each top-level test builds a single-core in-process cluster with the HTTP handler and DisableCache set, registers the userpass credential backend and the kv-v2 and totp logical backends, starts the cluster, waits for core 0 to become active, and defers cluster cleanup so the test leaves no running core behind.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A workflow whose single flow calls sys/workflows/execute of itself must fail execution with an error containing "too much workflow recursion" instead of looping.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Executing the login-MFA workflow provisions userpass, an admin policy, an identity entity and alias, a TOTP MFA method with a login enforcement, imports the generated TOTP URL into the totp mount, reads a code, and performs the login with the X-Vault-MFA header; the returned token must successfully read auth/token/lookup-self.

label: SpecRequirement
text: With AllowUnauthenticatedWorkflows true, a tokenless client may execute a workflow stored with allow_unauthenticated true via sys/workflows/unauthed-execute, but the same tokenless client must receive a "permission denied" error for a workflow stored with allow_unauthenticated false.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Writing a workflow definition to sys/workflows/manage/<name> makes it appear in the List of sys/workflows/manage and makes it executable at sys/workflows/execute/<name>; deleting it removes it so the List returns nil, and a fresh namespace starts with no workflows.

label: SpecRequirement
text: forwardedRequestRPCServer.CheckInvalidations registers the stream as an invalidation peer, returns the error `not registered; check active server's logs for information` when registration fails, and otherwise blocks on the peer stop channel until the stream is finished so the stream stays open while invalidations are delivered.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Handoff returns nil after warning and closing the TLS connection when the handler is not in HA mode; in HA mode it registers two wait-group units, closes the connection when any of quit channel, caller close channel, or the handler stop channel fires, and serves the connection through the HTTP/2 server with the gRPC server as handler.

label: SpecRequirement
text: forwardedRequestRPCServer.Echo caches an incoming node connection info entry keyed by cluster address when the request cluster address is non-empty, updates raft follower states only when the raft applied index is positive, the raft node id is non-empty and follower states are configured, and replies with message `pong` plus the core replication state and, when a raft backend exists, its applied index and node id.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each echo tick is bounded by a two second context timeout and stores the active node replication state from the reply after verifying a non-nil `pong` reply; each namespace key synchronization is bounded by a two minute context timeout and is guarded by an atomic boolean so overlapping syncs log a warning and return instead of running concurrently.

label: SpecRequirement
text: getKeys returns nil when the core reports no namespaces missing keys, requests those namespaces from the active node, returns nil when the reply carries no keys, and otherwise writes the returned batch back through core.SetNamespaceKeys, wrapping failures as `failed loading namespace keys`.

text: The kv paths list the "kv/" prefix through Storage.List and, for a generic key segment, declare key, value and version fields with an existence check that reports presence by whether Storage.Get returns a non-nil entry; the read callback returns the stored bytes as the value plus the requested version, create and update both write the value to the request path, and delete removes that path from storage.

text: The error paths expose errors/rpc and errors/kill as reads and errors/type as a create or update taking an integer err_type; a request without err_type returns rpc.ErrShutdown, and an err_type value selects one of the plugin error kinds — plain error, errutil.UserError, errutil.InternalError, logical.CodedError(403), logical.StatusBadRequest, ErrUnsupportedOperation, ErrUnsupportedPath, ErrInvalidRequest, ErrPermissionDenied or ErrMultiAuthzPending — each message being "test".

text: Backend returns a backend whose embedded framework.Backend registers, in one PathAppend, the error paths, the kv paths, and the internal, special and raw paths; declares PathsSpecial Unauthenticated as "special"; takes Invalidate from the backend's own invalidate method; ships an empty Secrets list; and reports BackendType logical.TypeLogical.

text: The backend's invalidate callback clears the backend's internal string field to the empty string when the invalidated key is "internal" and leaves it untouched for any other key, giving the framework's Invalidate hook an observable effect.
