text: A TLS connection state converts to a protobuf ConnectionState and back again, preserving version, handshake completion, negotiated protocol, server name, peer certificates, verified chains and the cipher suite.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.Connection converts to a protobuf Connection and back again, keeping the remote address, remote port and the embedded TLS connection state of the caller.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package's tests exercise the protobuf to logical translation functions so a change that breaks a round trip, drops a field, or changes error conversion fails the test suite.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.Request converts to a protobuf Request and back again, so operation, path, data, storage, auth, headers, client token, display name, connection info and mount metadata survive the plugin boundary; conversion reports an error when a logical value cannot be represented.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.Auth converts to a protobuf Auth and back again, carrying policies, metadata, lease options, internal data, display name, token type, alias and group aliases, boundary fields and token pieces across the boundary.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The Empty message implements the protobuf reflection contract: Reset zeroes the message, String renders the protobuf text form, ProtoMessage marks the type as a proto message, ProtoReflect returns the message state, and Descriptor returns the file descriptor bytes and message index.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.Response converts to a protobuf Response and back again, preserving data, the list of secret and auth entries, redirects, warnings, wrap info and the response's own secret and auth payloads.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package registers the Backend, Storage and SystemView gRPC services on a service registrar, each binding the service's full protobuf name to the supplied server implementation so a plugin host can serve the plugin over gRPC.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A single X.509 certificate converts to a protobuf Certificate and back again, preserving the ASN.1 DER bytes of the certificate.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The generated UnsafeBackendServer and UnsafeStorageServer interfaces carry the must-embed marker that tells implementers forward compatibility is not guaranteed, so servers embed the interface and keep compiling when the service gains methods.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Errors cross the boundary as ProtoError values: ErrToProtoErr encodes a Go error into a protobuf error, ProtoErrToErr rebuilds an error from a protobuf error, and ErrToString renders an error as a string; a nil error maps to a nil protobuf error and back to nil.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A slice of X.509 certificates converts to a protobuf CertificateChain and back again, so an ordered peer or verified chain keeps its length and order across the boundary.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.LeaseOptions converts to a protobuf LeaseOptions and back again, preserving the TTL, max TTL, renewable flag and increment value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.StorageEntry converts to a protobuf StorageEntry and back again, so the key, value bytes and seal-wrap flag survive storage traffic over the plugin link.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.TokenEntry converts to a protobuf TokenEntry and back again, so token identity, path, policies, metadata, expiry, role, namespace and bound CIDRs keep their values in both directions.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Request and response wrap info convert in both directions: a logical.RequestWrapInfo becomes a protobuf RequestWrapInfo and a ResponseWrapInfo becomes a protobuf ResponseWrapInfo, with TTL, token, accessor, creation time, creation path, wrapped accessor and seal-wrapping state preserved.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A logical.Secret converts to a protobuf Secret and back again, preserving lease options, internal data, lease identifier, renewable flag and the dynamic and raw secret markers.

label: SpecRequirement
text: New MUST return a *PriorityQueue whose heap slice and key map are both allocated empty, and the slice MUST be initialized through heap.Init so the queue is immediately usable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The unexported queue type MUST satisfy container/heap.Interface, with queue.Len reporting the slice length, queue.Swap exchanging elements in place, queue.Push appending an item, and queue.Pop removing the last element and clearing the vacated slot to avoid a memory leak.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Pop MUST return ErrEmpty when the queue holds no items, and otherwise MUST remove and return the highest priority item while deleting its key from dataMap.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The dataMap keyed by Item.Key MUST stay in sync with the heap slice at all times, so that after any Push, Pop or PopByKey the map length equals the slice length and every map value points at the item held in the slice.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PopByKey MUST return (nil, nil) when the key is absent, and when present MUST remove the item from the heap with heap.Remove using the item's stored index, delete the key from dataMap, and return the removed item.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Swap, queue.Push and queue.Pop MUST keep each Item's unexported index field equal to its position in the heap slice, since heap.Remove and heap.Fix locate items by that index; queue.Pop MUST set the removed item's index to -1.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Push MUST reject a nil item or an item with an empty Key by returning the error "error adding item: Item Key is required", and MUST reject a Key that is already in dataMap by returning ErrDuplicateItem rather than updating the existing entry.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Push MUST deep-copy the item with copystructure.Copy before storing it, so the queued entry and the dataMap entry are the clone and later modification of the caller's item cannot affect the queue.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every operation that touches the heap slice or the key map MUST hold the PriorityQueue mutex: Len takes a read lock, while Pop, Push and PopByKey take the write lock for their full body.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Item MUST expose Key as the unique string identifier, Value as an any-typed payload for callers, and Priority as the int64 ordering key, and MUST keep the heap bookkeeping index unexported so consumers cannot corrupt it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The package tests SHOULD assert heap.Interface conformance for queue at compile time and cover New leaving both structures empty, Push rejecting nil, duplicate and keyless items, Pop returning items in ascending priority together with their keys, PopByKey returning no error for a missing key, and the slice and map lengths agreeing after every mutation and drain.

label: SpecInterface
name: queue.Less
signature: func (q queue) Less(i, j int) bool

label: SpecRequirement
text: Ordering MUST be by Item.Priority as an int64 with the lowest value treated as highest priority; queue.Less compares q[i].Priority < q[j].Priority, and the priority of items with equal values is undetermined.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Because these files are a vendored copy of the OpenBao tooling, rule ids, severities, messages and the MPL-2.0 copyright and SPDX headers must stay as upstream defines them, so findings from this repository remain comparable with upstream and the license notice stays attached.

label: SpecRequirement
text: lock-not-unlocked-on-return.yml must define Go rules lock_not_unlocked and read_lock_not_unlocked at severity WARNING. Each matches a Lock() or RLock() followed later by an if-branch that returns, and reports the lock and condition metavariables. Both must suppress the case where the lock is released before that return, where it is released anywhere before the branch, where the unlock goes through a function value assigned from $LOCK.Unlock or $LOCK.RUnlock, where unlock is deferred (directly, inside the branch, or inside a deferred closure), and where an earlier defer already covers a reacquired lock.

label: SpecRequirement
text: physical-storage.yml must define Go rule physical-storage-bypass-encryption at severity WARNING. It matches Put calls on $CORE.physical and on $CORE.underlyingPhysical, and reports that encryption is bypassed by accessing physical storage directly.

label: SpecRequirement
text: self-equals.yml must define Go rule self-equals at severity ERROR, matching a value compared with itself through either == or !=, and report "Comparing with self".

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every rule in every file of this context must declare languages: [go], so the rule set never reports on the non-Go code vendored in the same tree.

label: SpecRequirement
text: replication-has-state.yml must define Go rules replication-state-should-use-IsPerfSecondary and replication-state-should-use-IsDrSecondar at severity WARNING, matching HasState with consts.ReplicationPerformanceSecondary and consts.ReplicationDRSecondary respectively. Each carries a fix that rewrites the call to $CORE.IsPerfSecondary() or $CORE.IsDRSecondary(), and each must not fire inside the defining IsPerfSecondary or IsDRSecondary method, nor on calls reached through $BACKEND.System() or $IDENTITYSTORE.localNode.

label: SpecRequirement
text: joinpath.yml must define Go rule use-strings-join-path at severity ERROR. It matches strings.Join where the separator argument is "/", "\\" or a backtick backslash, and its message asks whether path.Join() or filepath.Join() was intended.

label: SpecRequirement
text: replication-has-state.yml must also define replication-state-in-handler-op at severity WARNING, matching $B.System().ReplicationState().HasState($STATE) only when it sits inside a framework handler with the context, *logical.Request and *framework.FieldData parameters, telling the author to use the framework ForwardPerformance* setting; and replication-state-bad-logic at severity ERROR, matching a local-mount check OR-ed with a negation of the performance-standby replication state check and reporting invalid replication state handling of local mounts.

label: SpecRequirement
text: hostport.yml must define Go rule sprintf-host-port at severity ERROR. It matches fmt.Sprintf calls that build a host:port string, either the literal formats "%s:%s" and "%s:%d" or a dynamic format string matching "%s:[0-9]+", and only when the other metavariable name matches the case-insensitive regex .*(port|addr|host|listen|bind|ip). The reported message tells the author to use net.JoinHostPort instead.

label: SpecRequirement
text: logger-sprintf.yml must define Go rule logger-used-with-sprintf at severity WARNING. It matches a fmt.Sprintf argument passed to Trace, Debug, Info, Warn or Error on logger, on $PARENT.logger, and on $PARENT.Logger(), and reports that the logger message was generated by Sprintf.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Rule odd-sequence-ifs reports a second conditional whose test contradicts, repeats or loops on the test of an early-returning if, covering nested and sequential forms over both boolean and equality tests, at severity ERROR.

text: Rule hc-return-nil in return-nil.yml reports returning a variable from inside its own nil test, and returning that variable after an if that returns early when it is non-nil, at severity ERROR.

text: Rule bad-multierror-append reports go code that assigns multierror.Append back onto either operand, covering $ERR = multierror.Append($ERRORS, $ERR), $ERR = multierror.Append($ERR, $ERR), $ERRORS = multierror.Append($ERR, $ERR) and $ERRORS = multierror.Append($ERR, $ERRORS), at severity ERROR.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Rule hash-sum-without-write reports a hash Sum call on a freshly constructed hasher or on a hasher whose value never reaches a Write call or another function, at severity ERROR.

text: NamedPathAdapter.updateRecord delegates to the same _saveRecord path as create, because create and update share one endpoint and one verb.

text: Every adapter in this directory extends ApplicationAdapter from application.js, so all of them inherit urlPrefix, buildURL and the ajax request helper instead of calling the network directly.

text: NamedPathAdapter.findRecord backfills resp.data.name with the name supplied to findRecord when the response omits a name, so Ember Data does not reject a record pushed without an id.

text: NamedPathAdapter.createRecord throws `A record already exists with the name: ${name}` when store.peekRecord finds a record of the same model type and name, and only calls _saveRecord when no such record exists, so a create never silently overwrites an existing named record.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The directory keeps one adapter module per server resource family, covering auth methods, AWS and SSH credentials and roles, capabilities, cluster and server state, console, generated item lists, leases, nodes, permissions, policies, raft join, secret engines, KV v1 and v2 secrets and versions, SSH signing and OTP, tools, and transit keys, so each model type resolves to a dedicated adapter.

text: NamedPathAdapter fixes namespace to 'v1' and saveMethod to 'POST', and subclasses that need PUT override saveMethod rather than reimplementing the save path.

text: NamespaceAdapter.pathForType returns 'namespaces', so model URLs for namespaces are built under the namespaces path segment.

label: SpecRequirement
text: MfaMethodAdapter routes both create and update through createOrUpdate over its custom buildURL, and sends deletes to the URL produced by urlForDeleteRecord, so MFA method writes use one combined path instead of the default record URLs.

text: MfaSetupAdapter.currentTokenGenerate POSTs the given data to `/v1/identity/mfa/method/totp/generate` and returns the ajax promise, so TOTP enrollment for the current token does not go through Ember Data record plumbing.

text: NamespaceAdapter.query issues a GET to `/${urlPrefix}/namespaces?list=true` with no filter argument, so a namespace query always returns the full list.

label: SpecRequirement
text: NamedPathAdapter._saveRecord serializes the snapshot through the model serializer, sends the result to urlForUpdateRecord with the record name as id and saveMethod as verb, and resolves with the serialized data because the server response body is empty.

text: NamespaceAdapter.findAll forwards snapshot.adapterOptions.namespace to the request when that option is defined, and otherwise falls back to the superclass findAll, so a scoped listing carries the namespace option while an unscoped one uses the default request.

text: MfaSetupAdapter.adminDestroy POSTs the given data to `/v1/identity/mfa/method/totp/admin-destroy`, so destroying a TOTP method for another identity is sent as a POST to the admin endpoint.

text: NamespaceAdapter.urlForFindAll returns `/${urlPrefix}/internal/ui/namespaces` when snapshot.adapterOptions.forUser is set, and `/${urlPrefix}/namespaces?list=true` otherwise, so user-scoped scope listing uses the internal endpoint while the ordinary listing uses the LIST query form.

text: NamespaceAdapter creates a record with the namespace path taken from snapshot.attr('path') as both the URL id and the id of the returned payload object, because the create response carries no identifier of its own.

text: The azure, jwt, kubernetes, ldap, oidc and radius adapters each export `AuthConfig.extend()` with no property overrides, so all six inherit the base namespace, path derivation, URL building and create/update behavior unchanged.

text: `buildURL` resolves the backend id from the record id when present and otherwise from the record's `belongsTo('backend')` relationship, then builds `<namespace>/<backendId>/config`; only when the model name contains `aws` does it append `pathForType(modelName)` to that URL.

text: Only AWS auth models carry a per-type config sub-path, because AWS exposes several config endpoints; all other auth methods share the single `<backendId>/config` endpoint of the base adapter.

text: `pathForType` reduces the model type to its last `/`-separated segment, so namespaced model names resolve to the trailing type name; the two list-tidy types `identity-accesslist` and `roletag-denylist` are special-cased to `tidy/<type>` instead.

text: `createRecord` and `updateRecord` delegate to the superclass implementation and then resolve with `{ id }`, where `id` is the owning backend's id taken from `snapshot.belongsTo('backend')`, so callers receive the backend id rather than the server payload.

text: The shared auth-config adapter declares the API namespace `/v1/auth`, so every request it issues is rooted under that prefix.

text: Each of the three AWS adapter files MUST keep the HashiCorp copyright line and the MPL-2.0 SPDX identifier at the top of the file, since the files are vendored from the upstream OpenBao UI tree.

text: The aws/client.js adapter module MUST import the shared AuthConfig adapter from ../_base and export its extend() result unchanged, so the AWS client auth-config model resolves to an adapter with no behavior of its own.

text: The aws/identity-accesslist.js adapter module MUST import the shared AuthConfig adapter from ../_base and export its extend() result unchanged, so the identity accesslist model resolves to its own adapter class that inherits the base URL and record handling.

text: VersionHistoryAdapter.findAll must issue an HTTP GET through `this.ajax` to `this.buildURL()` concatenated with `/version-history`, pass the query data `{ list: true }`, and resolve with the response body exactly as received, without adding or renaming fields.

text: The client adapters for these endpoints should stay grouped under third_party/openbao/ui/app/adapters/clients, one adapter per file, with the activity adapter in activity.js and the version-history adapter in version-history.js; config.js belongs to the same directory.

text: ActivityAdapter.queryRecord must build the request URL as `this.buildURL()` concatenated with `/internal/counters/activity`, send it as an HTTP GET through `this.ajax` with the formatted time parameters as the request data, and only send the request when formatQueryParams returns a truthy value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ActivityAdapter.formatQueryParams must return an object with `start_time` and `end_time` as Unix second timestamps computed in UTC. When the incoming start_time or end_time already carries a `timestamp`, that value must be used unchanged; otherwise start_time must be the first day of the selected month, `Date.UTC(year, monthIdx, 1)`, and end_time must be the last day of the selected month, `Date.UTC(year, monthIdx + 1, 0)`, where a day of 0 rolls back to the final day of the previous month.

text: Both ActivityAdapter and VersionHistoryAdapter must extend ApplicationAdapter and reach the backend only through the inherited `this.buildURL` and `this.ajax` helpers, so that host resolution and request transport stay owned by the application adapter.

label: SpecRequirement
text: A single-role query must return the request annotated with its type, backend and id; when query.type is absent the adapter must request both static and dynamic roles and use the one that returned a value, merging its data into a response that records the resolved type.

text: The connection adapter must build URLs of the form <base>/<backend>/config when no id is given and <base>/<backend>/config/<id> when an id is given, and must special-case type 'ROTATE' to <base>/<backend>/rotate-root/<id> and type 'RESET' to <base>/<backend>/reset/<id>.

text: Every adapter in this context extends the shared ApplicationAdapter and sets namespace to 'v1', so all request URLs it builds are rooted at the v1 API prefix.

label: SpecRequirement
text: When the connection adapter fetches without an id, it must send a 'list' query parameter set to true so the engine returns the key list rather than a single configuration record.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The credential adapter must read static credentials from <base>/<backend>/static-creds/<secret> and dynamic credentials from <base>/<backend>/creds/<secret>, URL-encoding both the backend and the secret, and must tag each response with roleType 'static' or 'dynamic' respectively.

text: The credential adapter must expose rotateRoleCredentials(backend, id), issuing a POST to <base>/<backend>/rotate-role/<id> with both path segments URL-encoded.

text: Creating and updating a role must POST serializer output to the type-appropriate role URL and return a payload carrying the name as id, since the engine may answer 204 to a non-DELETE write.

text: The group adapter MUST provide a lookup method that POSTs the given data to /${urlPrefix}/identity/lookup/group, returning undefined when the response is falsy (an unsuccessful lookup is a 204) and otherwise normalizing the response with the identity/group serializer and pushing it into the store before returning the raw response.

text: The identity base adapter MUST override query to issue a GET request to buildURL with a null id for the queried model name, rather than letting Ember Data perform the default query request.

text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.query issues a list: true GET against the provider-scoped keys URL from the keymgmt/provider adapter when query.provider is set, otherwise against the backend-level key URL, and sets res.backend before resolving.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.url builds '<namespace>/<backend>/key' and, when an id is given, appends the path-encoded id; it appends '/rotate' when type is 'ROTATE' and '/kms' when type is 'PROVIDERS', and otherwise returns the plain id URL.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both keymgmt adapters declare the API namespace 'v1', so every generated request URL is prefixed with that version segment.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.getProvider GETs the key's 'kms' listing with list: true and returns the first name in data.keys, or null when the list is empty; it maps an HTTP 404 to null (not yet distributed) and an HTTP 403 to { permissionsError: true }, rethrowing any other error.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The keymgmt/provider adapter creates providers with a PUT rather than a POST, sending the serialized snapshot to the updateRecord URL, and returns the serialized data as the resolved value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.queryRecord GETs the single key, stamps id and backend onto its data, and unless query.recordOnly is true also attaches provider (when found without a permissions error) and distribution to the returned object.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.updateRecord PUTs to the key URL a payload containing only the 'deletion_allowed' and 'min_enabled_version' keys picked out of the serialized snapshot, so other attributes are never sent on update.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The keymgmt/provider adapter decorates findRecord responses by copying the lookup name into resp.data, and its query fetches every named key in the listing through findRecord using a mocked snapshot that answers only the 'backend' attribute, replacing data.keys with the full records and setting resp.backend.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The keymgmt/provider adapter maps pathForType to 'kms', rewrites the 'kms' segment to '<backend>/kms' in buildURL from the snapshot or query, and exposes buildKeysURL which appends '/<provider>/key' to a query-scoped provider URL.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.pathForType returns the literal 'key' and leaves the backend name out, because buildURL is responsible for prepending it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.getDistribution GETs '<backend>/kms/<kms>/key/<key>' and returns the response data with the comma-separated 'purpose' field split into a purposeArray.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.createRecord POSTs only the 'type' attribute to the key URL, then, only when snapshot.attr('deletionAllowed') is truthy, PUTs the update payload; if that update fails it throws an error stating the key was created but not all settings were saved. It resolves with the serialized data plus id (the name) and backend.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyAdapter.buildURL delegates to the ApplicationAdapter implementation and then replaces the 'key' segment with '<backend>/key', taking the backend from snapshot.attr('backend') when a snapshot is present and from query.backend otherwise.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesRoleAdapter extends NamedPathAdapter and builds role URLs as the adapter buildURL plus the encoded backend plus '/roles', appending the role name only when a name is given; urlForQuery resolves through that helper with the backend carried by the query object, and urlForUpdateRecord and urlForDeleteRecord resolve through it with the backend carried by the snapshot.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesConfigAdapter extends ApplicationAdapter and sets its namespace property to 'v1', so every request it builds is rooted at the versioned UI API namespace.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesConfigAdapter.queryRecord GETs the config URL for the queried backend and returns the raw response object with the backend name attached to it as a top-level backend property, so the caller can re-address the record.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesConfigAdapter.createRecord and updateRecord both forward their arguments to the private _saveRecord, which serializes the snapshot through the store serializer for the record's modelName, takes the URL id from snapshot.id falling back to the snapshot's backend attribute, POSTs the serialized data to that URL, and resolves with the serialized data spread together with backend and id both set to that id.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesRoleAdapter.generateCredentials builds <buildURL>/<encodePath(backend)>/creds/<data.role>, deletes the role field from the request data, POSTs the remaining data there, and resolves with one object holding lease_id, lease_duration and the flattened response data.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesRoleAdapter.queryRecord GETs the named role URL for the queried backend and returns the response data with backend and name written onto it, so the record is addressable after load.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesConfigAdapter.checkConfigVars GETs the 'check' subpath of the backend's config URL, so the UI can verify the mount's configuration variables without reading the config record itself.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesRoleAdapter.query GETs the roles collection URL with the data parameter list=true and maps each key of the response data to a role object carrying that key as name and the queried backend, so role lists are addressable per mount.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KubernetesConfigAdapter.getURL joins the adapter buildURL with the encoded backend mount path and a trailing path segment that defaults to 'config'; urlForUpdateRecord returns that config URL built from the snapshot's backend attribute, and urlForDeleteRecord returns it from the backend argument it is handed.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each OIDC adapter class is a default export that extends NamedPathAdapter from third_party/openbao/ui/app/adapters/named-path.js, so persistence behavior comes from the shared base and the adapter itself only narrows the path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcAssignmentAdapter.pathForType takes no arguments and returns the API path for the OIDC assignment resource, which the base adapter appends when building request URLs.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcProviderAdapter.pathForType takes no arguments and returns the literal string 'identity/oidc/provider', fixing the endpoint the provider model is persisted against.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcScopeAdapter.pathForType takes no arguments and returns the literal string 'identity/oidc/scope', fixing the endpoint the scope model is persisted against.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcClientAdapter.pathForType takes no arguments and returns the literal string 'identity/oidc/client', fixing the endpoint the client model is persisted against.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The assignment, client, provider and scope adapters stay free of extra methods or state, so all persistence behavior remains owned by NamedPathAdapter and only the key adapter adds an operation.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcKeyAdapter.pathForType takes no arguments and returns the API path for the OIDC key resource, which the base adapter uses as the collection path for key records.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcKeyAdapter.rotate is the only operation beyond the inherited CRUD in this context and accepts two arguments, the key name and verification_ttl, so rotation is addressed to a named key with a caller-supplied verification TTL.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiTidyAdapter.createRecord throws Error('Auto tidy type models are never new, please use findRecord') when adapterOptions.tidyType is 'auto'; otherwise it serializes the snapshot with that tidy type, POSTs to <backend>/tidy, and resolves a synthesized record with id set to the backend and type 'pki/tidy'.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiRoleAdapter and PkiSignIntermediateAdapter exist as the default exports for the pki role and sign-intermediate record families, giving those models their own HTTP adapter alongside the action, key, tidy and issuer adapters.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createRecord obtains the serializer for the model name from the store, resolves the URL through urlForCreateRecord, and POSTs the serialized snapshot to it so generation, import and rotation actions all flow through one write path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: _baseUrl returns <encoded backend>/keys when no id is given and <encoded backend>/key/<encoded id> when an id is given, so collection and single-record requests differ by path shape.

label: SpecRequirement
text: urlForCreateRecord picks the backend as adapterOptions.mount when present and otherwise snapshot.record.backend, throws when either backend or adapterOptions.actionType is missing, and then maps actionType onto an endpoint: import to issuers/import/bundle when useIssuer is set else config/ca; generate-root to issuers/generate/root/<type> when useIssuer is set else root/generate/<type>; generate-csr to issuers/generate/intermediate/<type> when useIssuer is set else intermediate/generate/<type>; sign-intermediate to issuer/<encoded issuerRef>/sign-intermediate; and rotate-root to root/rotate/<type>. Any other actionType fails the assert.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Backend mount names, key ids and issuer refs are passed through encodePath before being interpolated into URLs, so names containing URL-unsafe characters still address the right mount.

label: SpecRequirement
text: query and queryRecord load issuer records and getIssuerMetadata(store, type, query, response, id) normalizes the response payload, while updateRecord(store, type, snapshot) writes issuer changes back through the same backend-scoped URL.

label: SpecRequirement
text: updateRecord POSTs only the serialized key_name to the single-key URL; query GETs the collection URL with list=true; queryRecord GETs the single-key URL built from query.backend and query.id; deleteRecord removes the single key.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiIssuerAdapter derives the mount from the snapshot through _getBackend and builds issuer URLs through urlForQuery(backend, id), with optionsForQuery(id) supplying the request options, so issuer reads and writes are always scoped to the resolved backend.

label: SpecRequirement
text: _baseUrl returns the built URL joined with the encoded backend mount, and every tidy request appends either /tidy or /config/auto-tidy to that value.

label: SpecRequirement
text: deleteAllIssuers(backend) is exposed on the adapter and declared on the matching PkiIssuerAdapter type as deleteAllIssuers(backend: string), so callers can remove every issuer under one mount without enumerating records.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiTidyAdapter.updateRecord throws Error('Manual tidy type models are always new, please use createRecord') when adapterOptions.tidyType is 'manual'; otherwise it POSTs the serialized snapshot to <backend>/config/auto-tidy using the record id as the backend, and findRecord GETs the same config/auto-tidy path because only auto-tidy is ever read.

label: SpecRequirement
text: createRecord POSTs to <keys url>/import when adapterOptions.import is set and to <keys url>/generate/<record.type> otherwise; when the response is not an import and carries no data.key_id, the adapter injects key_id from the snapshot's keyName attribute so the record id stays stable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each PKI adapter sets namespace = 'v1' so that buildURL() prefixes every request path with the v1 API namespace, and the mount is appended to that base.

label: SpecInterface
name: PkiCertificateSignAdapter
signature: class PkiCertificateSignAdapter extends PkiCertificateBaseAdapter { urlForCreateRecord(modelName, snapshot) }

label: SpecRequirement
text: `PkiCertificateSignAdapter.urlForCreateRecord(modelName, snapshot)` reads `role` and `backend` from `snapshot.record`, throws `Error('URL for create record is missing required attributes')` when either is absent, and otherwise returns `${this.buildURL()}/${encodePath(backend)}/sign/${encodePath(role)}`.

label: SpecInterface
name: PkiCertificateGenerateAdapter
signature: class PkiCertificateGenerateAdapter extends PkiCertificateBaseAdapter { urlForCreateRecord(modelName, snapshot) }

label: SpecInterface
name: PkiCertificateBaseAdapter
signature: class PkiCertificateBaseAdapter extends ApplicationAdapter { namespace; getURL(backend, id); fetchByQuery(query); query(store, type, query); queryRecord(store, type, query); updateRecord(store, type, snapshot) }

label: SpecRequirement
text: The base certificate adapter declares `namespace = 'v1'`, so every request it builds is prefixed with the v1 API namespace.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `PkiCertificateGenerateAdapter` and `PkiCertificateSignAdapter` each extend `PkiCertificateBaseAdapter` and override only `urlForCreateRecord`, inheriting the v1 namespace, the query/queryRecord read path and the revoke-based `updateRecord` from the base.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `getURL(backend, id)` builds `${buildURL()}/${encodePath(backend)}` and appends `/cert/${id}` when an id is given, or `/certs` when it is not, so a list request and a single-certificate read differ only in that suffix and the backend path segment is always path-encoded.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `updateRecord(store, type, snapshot)` POSTs to `${buildURL()}/${encodePath(backend)}/revoke` with data `{ serial_number: serialNumber }` when the record has a serial number, else `{ certificate }`; revocation is the only way a certificate record is updated because revoking sets the revocationTime property. The resolved value is `{ data: { ...serialize(snapshot), ...response.data } }`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `fetchByQuery(query)` issues a GET against `getURL(backend, id)`, sending `{ list: true }` as data when no id is present and `{}` when one is, then sets `resp.data.backend` to the query's backend and, when an id was given, sets `resp.data.id` and `resp.data.serial_number` to that id before returning the response.

label: SpecRequirement
text: `PkiCertificateGenerateAdapter.urlForCreateRecord(modelName, snapshot)` reads `role` and `backend` from `snapshot.record`, throws `Error('URL for create record is missing required attributes')` when either is absent, and otherwise returns `${this.buildURL()}/${encodePath(backend)}/issue/${encodePath(role)}`.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Both `query(store, type, query)` and `queryRecord(store, type, query)` ignore the store and type and return `fetchByQuery(query)`, so listing and single-record loading share one code path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: updateRecord must serialize the snapshot and issue an HTTP POST with that serialized payload as data to _url(snapshot.record.id), so the record's id supplies the backend mount path.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiConfigAcmeAdapter, PkiConfigClusterAdapter, PkiConfigCrlAdapter and PkiConfigUrlsAdapter must extend PkiConfigBaseAdapter, keep namespace 'v1', and override only _url(backend), so find and update behavior stays inherited and identical across the four config endpoints.

label: SpecRequirement
text: findRecord must issue an HTTP GET to the URL produced by _url(backend) and must resolve with the response body's data property, not the raw response, so callers receive the record payload directly.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The four subclasses should import encodePath from vault/utils/path-encoding-helpers rather than hand-rolling path escaping, keeping encoding behavior consistent with the rest of the UI.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each _url(backend) must return this.buildURL() joined with the URL-encoded backend mount path and then the adapter's own fixed segment: /config/acme for ACME, /config/cluster for cluster, /config/crl for CRL, and /config/urls for URLs; the backend must be passed through encodePath so mounts containing reserved characters stay addressable.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PkiConfigBaseAdapter must extend the UI application adapter and declare namespace 'v1', so every PKI config request is issued under that API namespace.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each of the acl, egp, and rgp adapters must be produced by calling `extend()` on the shared policy adapter imported from `../policy`, so that all three inherit their request behavior from that single base adapter instead of redefining it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The three adapters must stay free of properties and method overrides, so that no policy-type-specific request behavior diverges between acl, egp, and rgp; any such behavior belongs in the shared base policy adapter.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each adapter file must keep the HashiCorp copyright header and the `SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0` line at the top of the file, since these files are vendored upstream sources.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each adapter module must expose the extended class as its default export, because Ember Data resolves the adapter for the acl, egp, and rgp models through that default export.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The database secrets engine UI is carried by DatabaseConnectionEdit for connection configuration, DatabaseRoleEdit and DatabaseRoleSettingForm for role definition and per-role settings, and GenerateCredentialsDatabase with GetCredentialsCard for issuing credentials for a role.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DateDropdown defaults currentDate to now, derives currentYear and currentMonthIdx, and offers the last five years with all months selectable. selectMonth(month, dropdown) disables the current year when the chosen month is later than the current month; selectYear(year, dropdown) caps selectable months at the current month when the current year is chosen; both close the dropdown. handleSubmit runs args.validateDate when provided, stores the returned error in invalidDate and aborts the submit when a date is invalid.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Every module under third_party/openbao/ui/app/components exports exactly one default Ember component class that its co-located template renders; other symbols stay module-private. The whole directory is an unmodified vendored copy of the upstream OpenBao UI, so edits must be minimal and deliberate because they diverge from upstream.

label: SpecRequirement
text: FlashMessageComponent renders a flash message with its severity and a dismissal action, and TokenExpireWarning surfaces a warning before the current token expires so the user can renew it.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The crypto tool pages are one component each: ToolHash hashes input, ToolLookup looks up a token, ToolRandom generates random bytes, ToolWrap wraps plaintext, ToolUnwrap unwraps a token, ToolRewrap re-wraps an existing token, and WrapTtlComponent supplies the TTL selection used by the wrap flows.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ConfigureAwsSecretComponent persists AWS secrets engine configuration: saveRootCreds(data, event) writes the root credentials, saveLease(data, event) writes the lease settings, and handleTtlChange(name, ttlObj) reconciles the submitted TTL object with the form state.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The secret v2 UI is split across SecretEdit for reading and editing a version, SecretCreateOrUpdate for write paths, SecretEditMetadata for custom metadata and SecretEditToolbar, SecretVersionMenu and SecretDeleteMenu for toolbar actions, version selection and deletion; together they must cover create, update, read, version switch, metadata edit and destroy for a KV v2 secret.

label: SpecRequirement
text: OidcConsentBlockComponent renders the consent request shown during an OIDC authorisation flow and submits the client's allow or deny decision.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PolicyFormComponent edits a policy name and body and submits them to the policy endpoint, reporting validation errors before the request is sent.

label: SpecRequirement
text: MountBackendForm collects the mount type, path and options and submits the enable-mount request, and MountAccessorSelect lists mount accessors so a caller can filter by mount.

label: SpecRequirement
text: CalendarWidget keeps currentDate, calendarDisplayDate, showCalendar, tooltipTarget and tooltipText as state; it derives startDate, endDate, displayYear and the disableFutureYear and disablePastYear bounds from them, builds the month grid with widgetMonths, and reacts to addTooltip, removeTooltip, addYear, subYear, toggleShowCalendar, handleDateShortcut(dropdown, { target }) and selectMonth(month, dropdown) by moving the displayed month or toggling the popup.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ConfigureSshSecretComponent exposes delete() to remove the SSH engine configuration and saveConfig(event) to write it back from the submitted form.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SecretLink and ToolbarSecretLink render navigation to a secret at a given backend path, carrying the query parameters the target route needs, and must not mutate the store while rendering the link.

label: SpecRequirement
text: SplashPage, SectionTabs, SelectableCard, HoverCopyButton and GeneratedItemList provide reusable presentation: the splash layout, a tab bar over routed sections, a selectable card tile, a copy control that appears on hover, and a rendered list of generated items.

label: SpecRequirement
text: PaginationControls turns the list args (page, page size and total) into page navigation and reports page changes to its caller, and RegexValidator checks a value against the configured pattern and surfaces whether the value matched.

label: SpecRequirement
text: auth-form.js drives login by rendering the auth methods offered by the backend and dispatching the chosen method, auth-jwt.js and auth-form-options.js render the JWT/OIDC and method-option variants of that form, and b64-toggle.js toggles base64 display of a value in the auth payload.

label: SpecRequirement
text: DiffVersionSelector tracks leftSideVersionDataSelected, leftSideVersionSelected, rightSideVersionDataSelected, rightSideVersionSelected, statesMatch and visualDiff on the secret-v2-version adapter. It initialises the left side at the model's currentVersion and the right side at rightSideVersionInit, which is currentVersion minus one and 0 when currentVersion is 1; both queries resolve to null on failure rather than rejecting. The constructor calls createVisualDiff, which feeds the selected or initial version data through jsondiffpatch to produce the visual diff.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The options component's saveModel task must build the payload by serializing this.model.config, then assign this.model.description onto it, and must delete the token_type key when this.model.methodType equals 'token' because token_type is not tuneable for the token auth method.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The options saveModel task must call this.model.tune(data) with that payload; on an AdapterError it must return without rethrowing and must attempt to set this.model.errorMessage to err.errors[0] because model.save is not called and the model would otherwise never receive the error, wrapping that assignment so a failure is ignored; on any non-AdapterError it must rethrow.

label: SpecRequirement
text: On a successful tune the options component must call transitionToSafe with the router and route 'vault.cluster.access.methods' and then call flashMessages.success with 'The configuration was saved successfully.', matching the base component's post-save behavior.

label: SpecRequirement
text: options.js must import AuthConfigBase from './config' and export a component created by extending it, injecting its own flashMessages and router services.

label: SpecRequirement
text: AuthConfigBase.saveModel must be an ember-concurrency task wrapped in waitFor that yields this.model.save(); on error it must return silently when the error is an AdapterError and rethrow it otherwise; on success it must call transitionToSafe with the router and route 'vault.cluster.access.methods', then call flashMessages.success with 'The configuration was saved successfully.'.

label: SpecRequirement
text: AuthConfigBase must declare the static positionalParams list as ['model'], so the model is passed positionally when the component is invoked.

label: SpecRequirement
text: AuthConfigBase must be an Ember Component subclass with tagName set to the empty string, a model property defaulting to null, and injected flashMessages and router services.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The extended class must declare `attributeBindings: ['type']` so that a `type` property passed to the component renders as the `type` HTML attribute on the trigger element, letting a button trigger inside a form be set to `type="button"` instead of defaulting to submit.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The subclass should add no properties or methods beyond the `attributeBindings` override, keeping this file a minimal vendored passthrough of the addon trigger so addon upgrades stay cheap.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The file must keep the HashiCorp copyright notice and the `SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0` header comment, since it is vendored third-party source under the third_party tree.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The module's default export must be an Ember component class produced by calling `extend` on the default export of `ember-basic-dropdown/components/basic-dropdown/trigger`, so the local component inherits the addon trigger's dropdown open, close, and focus behavior unchanged.

label: SpecRequirement
text: The console component directory MUST contain the seven modules command-input.js, log-json.js, log-list.js, log-object.js, log-text.js, output-log.js and ui-panel.js, each responsible for its named part of rendering the console and its log output.

label: SpecRequirement
text: log-object.js MUST export stringifyObjectValues(data). It iterates the own enumerable keys of data with Object.keys, and for each key replaces the value with JSON.stringify(value) when typeof value is not 'string', leaving string values untouched.

label: SpecRequirement
text: output-log.js MAY render the accumulated console output, with the per-type log components (log-json, log-list, log-object, log-text) handling the individual entries that the output log collects.

label: SpecRequirement
text: log-object.js SHOULD use stringifyObjectValues on the log data it renders, so that non-string values reaching the object log view are shown as JSON text instead of raw objects.

label: SpecRequirement
text: stringifyObjectValues MUST mutate the caller's data object in place and MUST NOT return a new object: each converted value is assigned back onto the same key of the same object, and the function returns nothing.

label: SpecRequirement
text: ui-panel.js MAY act as the container that holds command-input.js and output-log.js together in the console panel.

label: SpecRequirement
text: lookup-input.js takes a public type of either 'entity' or 'group' that selects the store adapter identity/<type>, and its data() underscores the param name into the query key and additionally sets alias_mount_accessor whenever param is 'alias name'; init loads all auth-method records and defaults aliasMountAccessor to the first method's accessor.

label: SpecRequirement
text: popup-policy.js extends the popup base and reads params[0] as model and params[1] as policyName; its transaction sets model.policies to that collection with policyName removed via without(), saves the model, and reports 'Successfully removed '{policyName}' policy from {model.id}' or a problem-removing message.

label: SpecRequirement
text: popup-metadata.js extends the popup base and reads params[0] as model and params[1] as key; its transaction deletes metadata[key], reassigns the metadata object to a shallow copy to preserve reactivity, and saves the model, reporting removal or failure of that key.

label: SpecRequirement
text: popup-members.js extends the popup base and reads its three arguments from params as model, groupArray and memberId; its transaction removes memberId from the named group array on the model with without() and saves the model, reporting 'Successfully removed '{memberId}' from the group' or a problem-removing message.

label: SpecRequirement
text: entity-nav.js exports a Component with no properties, computed values, actions or injected services, so it exists only as a template-backed navigation placeholder.

label: SpecRequirement
text: popup-alias.js extends the popup base, derives messageArgs as [model.identityType, model.id], and implements transaction as model.destroyRecord(), reporting 'Successfully deleted {type}: {id}' or a problem-deleting message built from e.errors joined by a space or e.message.

label: SpecRequirement
text: edit-form.js exposes a save ember-concurrency task wrapped in waitFor and marked drop(), which yields model.save(), flashes the computed message on success and invokes the onSave callback with { saveType: 'save', model }; its deleteItem action calls model.destroyRecord() and then invokes onSave with { saveType: 'delete', model }; willDestroy rolls back the model's attributes when it is dirty and not already destroyed or destroying, ignoring teardown failures.

label: SpecRequirement
text: item-details.js injects flashMessages and its enable action sets the model's disabled flag to false, saves the model, and on resolution flashes `Successfully enabled entity: ${model.id}`; on rejection it joins e.errors with a space (falling back to e.message) into a problem message.

label: SpecRequirement
text: edit-form.js supports the modes create, edit and merge against a model with identityType, and its cancelLink computed property maps the `${mode}-${model.identityType}` key to a vault.cluster.access.identity route, falling back to the merge-entity-alias route when no model is present; getMessage builds a humanized success string, returning 'Successfully merged entities' for merge mode.

label: SpecRequirement
text: Each popup subclass extends the popup base, supplies its own messageArgs and transaction override, and reports its own successMessage and errorMessage, so the base contract's asserting transaction is never reached and the confirm-then-mutate flow is identical across alias deletion, member removal, metadata removal and policy removal.

label: SpecRequirement
text: _popup-base.js defines the shared popup contract: tagName is empty, flashMessages is injected, params defaults to null, onSuccess is a no-op and onError rolls back the model when it has rollbackAttributes; transaction is declared but asserts false so every subclass must override it; the performTransaction action spreads its arguments into messageArgs, calls transaction, and on resolve calls onSuccess then flashes successMessage, while on reject it calls onError then flashes errorMessage through flashMessages.success.

label: SpecRequirement
text: lookup-input.js exposes a lookup ember-concurrency task that calls adapter.lookup(store, data()); on error it flashes a danger message naming the type and error, on a falsy response it flashes a danger message stating no identity of that type was found for the param value, and on a response it transitions through transitionToSafe to the vault.cluster.access.identity.show route with the response id and the 'details' segment.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtDistribute.validMatchError returns null while either providerType or keyModel.type is unset, returns null when VALID_TYPES_BY_PROVIDER[providerType] contains keyModel.type, and otherwise returns an error keyed on 'key' when the @provider argument is supplied (field hidden) or keyed on 'provider' when it is not, with the trailing 'or change the key type' clause added only when @key is absent.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtDistribute.disableOperations is truthy when validMatchError is set, when formData.provider is empty, when formData.key is empty, or when an unsaved new key has no type, so the operation checkboxes stay disabled until a compatible key/provider pairing is complete.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtDistribute.createDistribution prevents the default event, flashes a danger message listing key, provider and operations as all required when formatData yields null, saves keyModel first when the key is new (flashing danger with the create error and aborting on failure), then calls distributeKey and finally re-queries the keymgmt/key record so distribution info is reloaded.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtDistribute.formatData returns null unless key, provider and a non-empty operations array are all present, and otherwise returns the payload { key, provider, purpose, protection } where purpose is the operations joined with commas, matching the shape the distribution endpoint expects.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtProviderEdit.onDelete destroys the provider model and then transitions to the root argument's path with the root model and query param tab='provider'; onDeleteKey destroys the passed key model and removes it from the provider model's keys collection; both flash a danger message built from joined error strings on failure.

label: SpecRequirement
text: KeymgmtKeyEdit.deleteKey destroys the model record and then transitions to the secrets backend list-root route using the model's backend, flashing a danger message if the destroy rejects.

label: SpecRequirement

intent: This context exists so the AppRole credential backend can run as an out-of-process OpenBao plugin binary. It isolates the harness boilerplate — flag parsing, TLS provider derivation, and multiplexed serving — from the backend implementation, which lives in the parent `approle` package and is reached only through the `approle.Factory` symbol. Keeping this file thin means the backend stays testable and buildable without the plugin harness, while the binary itself remains compileable against host versions that predate plugin AutoMTLS.

name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-healthcheck

name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-routing

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-adapters-auth-config

name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-token

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-cassandra-cassandra-database-plugin

intent: The context exists to pin down the observable contract of the exec test app so that the agent exec server behavior it verifies stays describable: which flags configure the process, how long it may live, how it reacts to signals, what it serves over HTTP, and what exit code it reports. name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agent-exec-test-app

name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-testhelpers-seal

intent: This context exists so backend database plugins and storage code in OpenBao can run small parameterised SQL statements without repeating prepare, execute, and resource-release boilerplate. The package isolates the template substitution of {{name}} tokens behind an unexported parseQuery helper, so no caller must do string replacement on SQL by hand. Only the four Execute* entry points are exported; parseQuery and execute stay internal to the file.

name: third-party-openbao-sdk-helper-dbtxn

intent: This context exists to specify the behavior of the MFA login enforcement detail/index controller in Openbao's UI: how it tracks the selected tab, how it renders and dismisses the delete confirmation, and what the delete action must do on success and on failure. name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-mfa-enforcements-enforcement

name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-testhelpers-mysql

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-adapters-pki-certificate

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-kubernetes-integrationtest-kind

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-kubernetes

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-instance-initializers

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-models-auth-config-aws

name: third-party-openbao-sdk-helper-identitytpl

intent: This context exists to pin down the deploy/examples/atproto/market example as an executable specification of what the kcp deno runtime must support: peer services that reach each other only by cluster-local name over TLS, with identity and certificates supplied from outside the pod, and a market bidder that reaches those same peers the same way. name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest-vault

name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-router

name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-barrier

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-oidc-keys

name: third-party-openbao-github-actions-set-up-go

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-secrets-backend

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-valkey-valkey-database-plugin

name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-stubbolt

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-components-sidebar-header

name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-testhelpers-pluginhelpers

name: third-party-openbao-sdk-physical-inmem

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-macros

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-kv-cmd-kv

name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agentproxyshared-sink-mock

name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-pkiext

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-mfa

name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-oidc-providers

name: third-party-openbao-github

name: third-party-openbao-sdk-database-dbplugin-v5-proto

label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-adapters-kubernetes

name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-quotas

label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-metrics

intent: The context exists so the agent exec server's contract is described independently of the surrounding OpenBao agent: which configuration the server accepts, how it derives runner state from environment templates, under what conditions it restarts or stops the child process, what it returns on cancellation, template error and child exit, and how restart-on-secret-changes values are interpreted. name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agent-exec

label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-sdk-helper-ldaputil

intent: This context exists to pin down the contract of the cert plugin's binary entry point: the sequence of flag parsing, TLS material derivation from the plugin API client meta, and the multiplexed serve call that registers `cert.Factory` as the backend factory. It matters because the entry point is the boundary between the plugin process and the OpenBao/Vault plugin protocol, and because the explicit `TLSProviderFunc` is what keeps the plugin loadable by older Vault versions without AutoMTLS. It also fixes the failure behavior — log and exit non-zero — so a failed serve is never silently ignored. The context deliberately holds no business logic: everything about certificate auth lives in the cert package, and this file must stay a thin bootstrapper.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-cert-cmd-cert

intent: This context exists so the OpenBao binary can name itself. Every component that prints, logs, or transmits a version — the HTTP audit backend's User-Agent, the CLI commands, the sys/health endpoint, service registration, and the seal-status API — calls into this package instead of hardcoding a string. It separates the injected build facts (ldflags variables) from the presentation rules, so a single place decides how a commit, a prerelease tag, vendor metadata, and a commit date combine into a user-visible version string.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-version

intent: This context exists to record the vendored OpenBao SDK priority queue that this repository carries under third_party, so that its contract, its exported surface and its locking and copy semantics are described from the code as it stands rather than inferred. It matters because the package is third-party code retained verbatim except for the queue import path, and anything that consumes it needs to know that ordering is lowest-int64-wins, that keys are unique and immutable once pushed, that pushes clone their input, and that every public operation is mutex-guarded.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-sdk-queue

intent: This context exists so the raft configuration behaviour exercised by the shared external raft test suite is also covered against real docker-hosted vault nodes driven by a locally built binary, rather than only in-process nodes. It guards the join and reconfiguration path: the cluster must behave correctly both before and after a node is added, and the test only runs where a binary path is supplied, so developers without docker or a built binary get a skip instead of a failure.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-raft-raft-binary

intent: This context exists to describe the vendored OpenBao AppRole auth-method package that deno-kcp carries under `third_party/openbao`, so its public surface (constructor, functional options, `Login`) and its documented behavior (single secret-ID source, late resolution of file and environment values, bounded file read, optional wrapping-token unwrap, write to `auth/<mountPath>/login`) are recorded as requirements rather than re-derived from source on each change. It anchors the contract other parts of the repository rely on when authenticating to OpenBao with a role ID and secret ID, and it marks the package as upstream code whose behavior is already exercised by its own tests.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-api-auth-approle

intent: This context exists so the MySQL database backend can be shipped and executed as a separate process that OpenBao talks to over the dbplugin RPC protocol. The main.go entrypoint isolates only the composition step: construct the MySQL plugin with the standard (non-legacy) username template and register it with ServeMultiplex. Keeping this as its own binary lets the MySQL engine be built, versioned, and mounted independently of the OpenBao server binary, with the legacy username template variant living in a sibling plugin directory.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-mysql-mysql-database-plugin

intent: This context exists so the agent proxy can run as a native Windows service. The Windows service manager drives the process through a handler interface, but the rest of the agent only needs one portable signal: a channel that fires when the service controller asks the process to stop. ShutdownChannel is that portable surface, and serviceWindows.Execute is the adapter that translates Windows service control requests into it. The init hook keeps normal interactive invocations unaffected, registering the handler only in a real service session.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-command-agentproxyshared-winsvc

intent: This context exists to describe the standalone, self-contained main package that OpenBao builds into the influxdb-database-plugin binary. It matters because the plugin is compiled and shipped as a separate process that OpenBao's database secrets engine launches and talks to over the dbplugin RPC interface; the entry point is the entire build target. Knowing that Run is a thin wrapper over dbplugin.ServeMultiplex(influxdb.New) fixes the contract: the plugin has no configuration of its own at startup, no flags, and no error paths, and all InfluxDB-specific behavior (connection handling, credential templating, user lifecycle) lives in the imported influxdb package rather than here.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-database-influxdb-influxdb-database-plugin

intent: This context exists to specify the six MFA component classes that the OpenBao UI uses to satisfy a login MFA challenge and to configure MFA methods and login enforcements. It captures the observable behaviour of each class — the constraint resolution and passcode validation of the login form, the two enrollment wizard steps, the method edit modal state machine, and the login enforcement form's target flattening, auth-method lookup and enforcement caching — so that these third-party components are described by what the code actually does rather than by the upstream templates that render them.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-components-mfa

intent: This context exists so command entrypoints across OpenBao can accept PGP recipients uniformly: operators name key files or keybase users on the command line, the package resolves them to entities, encrypts each share to its recipient, and reports fingerprints that operators verify out of band. It is a third-party vendored dependency under third_party/openbao, described so the surrounding repository can reason about its contract without re-reading the upstream source.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-helper-pgpkeys

intent: This context exists to describe the behaviour of the OIDC key detail controller in the vendored OpenBao UI, so that the rotate and delete flows for a single OIDC key are specified in one place. It matters because these two actions mutate key material and delete it: rotation must pass both the key name and the verification TTL to the adapter, and deletion must leave the record consistent (rollback on failure) and navigate away only after a successful destroy. The context gives the controller's service dependencies and its success/error reporting contract, which is what any change to the OIDC key detail screen has to preserve.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-oidc-keys-key

intent: This context exists so the Kubernetes service-registration client and retry handler can be tested without a real cluster. Server gives tests a live HTTP endpoint that mimics the Kubernetes pod API, State lets tests assert which patches arrived, and Conf supplies the client configuration pointing at that endpoint. It is a test-support package, so its contract is what the OpenBao kubernetes client tests depend on.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-serviceregistration-kubernetes-testing

intent: The context exists so the repository has a single, implementation-agnostic description of how a node advertises its state to a service registry. Callers in the vault and command layers depend on the interface and the Factory type rather than on any specific registry backend, so a Kubernetes implementation, a test double, or a future backend can be substituted at configuration time. Reading this context tells you what a registry integration must provide: construct from config plus logger plus initial State, start with a shutdown channel and wait group, and accept per-dimension state change notifications that report errors back to the core.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-serviceregistration

intent: This context exists so that the raft external tests have a reusable, cluster-agnostic assertion for Raft configuration state instead of each test spelling out the sys/storage/raft/configuration parse and leader checks itself. The helper parameterizes the cluster as a testcluster.VaultCluster, so any cluster implementation the test suite builds can be handed to it, and it derives the expected membership from cluster.Nodes() rather than from a literal list, which keeps the expectation correct as the node count changes. The two test files exist to invoke that helper (TestRaft_Configuration) and to exercise autopilot behavior against the same cluster shape; the context is defined by the shared assertion, not by the individual test names.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-raft

intent: This context exists so the userpass credential backend can be run as a separate process under OpenBao's plugin multiplexing protocol, which is how a plugin binary is launched and handed a listener and TLS material by the host. It is the process boundary: everything about the backend's behavior is elsewhere, but the backend cannot be loaded at all without this main package parsing the plugin API client flags, constructing the TLS provider function that keeps backwards compatibility with hosts lacking plugin AutoMTLS, and serving userpass.Factory over multiplex. The error path exists so a failure to serve is reported and turned into a nonzero exit rather than a silent hang.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-userpass-cmd-userpass

intent: Expose a small, dependency-light set of helpers so tests can render a struct or map into a stable, comparable representation without hand-writing per-type conversion code. The SHA-256 hashing of byte slices keeps binary values such as keys and tokens out of test output and gives a deterministic, fixed-width rendering, which makes golden comparisons and log lines safe to read and diff.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-sdk-helper-testhelpers

intent: This context exists to pin down the policy-name handling contract for the vendored OpenBao SDK helper: how raw policy input (nil, CSV string, or slice) becomes a canonical, deduplicated list, how root and default are treated, and how two policy lists are judged equivalent. It is the reference for any caller in deno-kcp that reads, stores, or diffs policy names and needs the same normalization rules the upstream SDK applies.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-sdk-helper-policyutil

intent: The context exists to specify the Transit logical backend that the repository vendors from OpenBao: what the plugin factory must construct, how the policy cache is sized from storage, how policies are fetched under locks, how the external key factory bridges to the system view, and which Transit API paths and batch request/response shapes the backend must serve. It gives the contract for the transit package so that consumers and refactors can rely on the exported entry points and the path surface without re-reading every file.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-logical-transit

intent: The package exists so OpenBao's seal-migration behavior can be exercised end to end against real test clusters. Each ParamTest* function is a scenario that a caller's test file invokes, parameterized by logger, reusable storage and a base port, so the same migration logic runs over different storage backends. The pre-1.4 and post-1.4 variants exist because the migration protocol changed at that version, and the transit-to-transit variant covers moving between two transit seals.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-sealmigration

intent: The context exists so the OIDC client details screen has a controller with a single destructive action: deleting the OIDC application being viewed. It is the UI-facing counterpart of the OIDC client read/delete path, kept separate from the list and creation screens so the details route can own deletion, user feedback, and post-delete navigation. Anyone changing how OIDC clients are deleted, how deletion errors are reported, or where the user lands after a delete must look here.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access-oidc-clients-client

intent: This context exists to record the observable contract of the two vendored OpenBao UI controllers in the vault/cluster/access folder, so that the auth-methods list filtering behavior and the OIDC header state machine can be referenced, tested or modified without re-reading the Ember source. It names the state each controller owns, the derived values it computes from the route model, and the route-name conditions that drive the OIDC header.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-controllers-vault-cluster-access

intent: This context exists so the Raft physical storage package of the vendored OpenBao code has a written specification of its FSM and log-application contract: what an applied entry means, how transaction errors travel back through the log, how the Bolt-backed FSM is opened, how apply delay is injected for tests, and which size limits reject an entry before it is proposed. It anchors those rules to the concrete files and functions that implement them so later edits to deno-kcp's third_party subtree can be checked against behaviour rather than against memory of upstream OpenBao.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-physical-raft

intent: The context exists to pin down the behaviour of the OIDC form components as a specification: which args they read from the model, which tracked state they expose for validation and error display, how the allow_all/limited selection is translated into wildcard list values on save, which TTL fields are defaulted, and how the two callbacks are fired. The components are a vendored third_party OpenBao UI subtree inside deno-kcp, so the intent is to describe the code as it stands rather than to propose changes to it.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-components-oidc

intent: The context exists to specify the Kubernetes auth method client helper so that callers and reimplementations know the exact constructor contract, option semantics, error strings, and login entry point. It pins down which behaviors are required of NewKubernetesAuth and of each LoginOption so that the Kubernetes backend login can be constructed and exercised against an *api.Client without reading the source. It also records that LoginOption here is a per-package type, not shared with the approle, ldap, or userpass packages.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-api-auth-kubernetes

intent: The context exists to verify, from outside the vault core, that the irrevocable-lease reporting surface of the expiration subsystem behaves correctly end to end over HTTP: that sys/leases/count and sys/leases report zero leases on a fresh cluster, report the exact injected count and per-mount breakdown after injection, and that sys/leases applies the default return cap with its warning until the caller passes limit=none. It is the external acceptance layer for the irrevocable lease listing and counting endpoints, so it pins the response shape (lease_count, counts, leases, mount_id, warnings) that API consumers depend on.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-expiration

intent: This context exists to give integration tests of the Kubernetes auth backend a way to talk to a Vault/OpenBao instance that runs inside a Kubernetes pod. Because the container is not reachable directly from the test host, the package provides the two primitives the tests need: an authenticated clientset built from a caller-named kubeconfig context, and a port-forward that exposes the pod's Vault port 8200 on a free local port, together with a close function so the tunnel can be torn down. Both helpers share the same kubeconfig resolution path, and every failure is returned as a wrapped error naming the step that failed, so a broken test setup reports where it broke.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest-k8s

intent: This context exists to verify that the sys/pprof endpoints behave the same way on a real OpenBao server process as they do on the fake test cluster used by the sibling pprof package. The two tests are deliberately thin: they only build the exec dev cluster, wire the binary path and listen address, and hand the cluster to the shared pprof test bodies, because the mechanism under test is the exec-based cluster, not the pprof assertions themselves. The BAO_BINARY gate keeps the suite from failing on machines without a built server binary.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-pprof-pprof-binary

intent: This context is the trigger decider, the piece of the deno-kcp control plane that turns a finished policy workflow run into a deno job. It exists so the RunTrigger reconciliation decision is testable and side-effect free: the reconciler decides, and the provider layer acts. When the referenced run succeeds and its outputs match the trigger's match map, the decider asks for a job named <trigger>-<run> and records the run as consumed so the same run never fires twice; cancelled, failed, or unfinished runs leave the trigger pending or skipped. Deletion is handled by asking for finalizer removal.
label: SpecContext
name: internal-trigger

intent: This context documents the two client-side adapter modules that let the OpenBao UI speak to the key-management secrets engine over HTTP. It exists so the request shapes, URL construction, allowed attribute sets, and error/empty-state handling of the keymgmt key and provider adapters are stated explicitly and can be validated against the code, rather than inferred from the Ember model layer or the Go HTTP handlers on the server side.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-ui-app-adapters-keymgmt

intent: This context exists to pin down the observable contract of the response-header allow-list in the vendored third_party/openbao vault HTTP handler, independent of this repository's own code: a plugin mount must not be able to leak arbitrary HTTP response headers to clients, and an operator must be able to opt a specific header back in per mount through the allowed_response_headers tuning, including when the configured casing differs from the emitted casing. Because the file is an external black-box test that speaks only over the HTTP API (client.Logical().ReadRaw, client.Sys().TuneMount) and not over internal Go packages, it documents the behaviour the vendored handler is expected to preserve across upstream updates rather than behaviour authored in this repo.
label: SpecContext
name: third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-response

intent: This context exists so the rest of deno-kcp can host and drive OpenBao plugins without depending on an out-of-tree copy of the SDK. It fixes the plugin-side contract: how the host learns whether a plugin supports multiplexing, how a plugin reads the mlock and metadata-mode environment flags, how run options are assembled into a go-plugin client, and which interfaces a caller must supply (Looker, RunnerUtil, PluginClient) or consume (PluginRunner).
